source_units.text: He cried into my ears with a loud voice, saying, “The city’s retribution has drawn near.” Each had the implements of destruction in his hand.

And behold, six men came from the direction of the high gate facing north, each with an axe in his hand. One man among them wore a full-length robe, with a sapphire belt at his waist. They entered and stood beside the bronze altar.
The glory of the God of Israel, which had been upon the cherubim, rose from them to the forecourt of the house. He called the man wearing the full-length robe, who had the belt at his waist,
and said to him, “Pass through the midst of Jerusalem and put the sign upon the foreheads of the men who sigh deeply and grieve over all the lawlessness being committed within her.”
To these others He said while I listened, “Go behind him into the city and strike. Do not spare with your eyes, and have no mercy.

Old man, young man, maiden, infants and women—kill them to obliteration. But do not approach anyone upon whom the sign is. Begin at My holy places.” They began with the elderly men who were inside the house.
He said to them, “Defile the house and fill the roads with the dead as you go out, and strike.”
As they struck, I fall upon my face and cried aloud and said, “Alas, Lord! Art Thou obliterating the survivors of Israel as Thou pourest out Thy wrath upon Jerusalem?”

He said to me, “The injustice of the house of Israel and Judah has grown very, very great, because the land is full of many peoples, and the city full of injustice and uncleanness. For they said, ‘The Lord has abandoned the land; the Lord does not look upon it.’
My eye will not spare, nor will I have mercy. I have brought their ways upon their heads.”
And behold, the man wearing the full-length robe, with the belt fastened at his waist, answered, saying, “I have done as Thou didst command me.”
I saw, and behold, above the firmament over the cherubim’s head was something like sapphire stone, a throne’s likeness above them.
He said to the man wearing the robe, “Go in among the wheels beneath the cherubim, fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim, and scatter them over the city.” He went in before me.
The cherubim stood to the right of the house as the man entered, and the cloud filled the inner court.
The Lord’s glory departed from the cherubim to the forecourt of the house. The cloud filled the house, and the court filled with the radiance of the Lord’s glory.
The sound of the cherubim’s wings was heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Shaddai speaking.
When He commanded the man wearing the holy robe, saying, “Take fire from among the wheels, from among the cherubim,” he entered and stood beside the wheels,
and he stretched out his hand into the midst of the fire among the cherubim, took it and gave it into the hands of the man wearing the holy robe. He took it and went out.
I saw the cherubim, the likeness of human hands beneath their wings.
I saw, and behold, four wheels stood beside the cherubim, one wheel beside one cherub. The wheels’ appearance was like the appearance of a carbuncle stone.
Their appearance was one likeness for all four, as when a wheel is within a wheel.
As they went, they went toward their four directions; they did not turn as they went. For wherever the one leading part looked, they went, and they did not turn as they went.
Their backs, their hands, their wings, and the wheels were full of eyes all around, upon their four wheels.
These wheels were called “Gelgel” in my hearing.
The cherubim lifted themselves. This was the living creature I had seen at the river Chebar.
When the cherubim went, the wheels went beside them. When the cherubim raised their wings to rise from the earth, their wheels did not turn.
When they stood, these stood; when they rose, these rose with them, because a spirit of life was in them.
The Lord’s glory went out from the house and mounted upon the cherubim,

and the cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the earth before me as they went out, with the wheels beside them. They stood at the entrance of the opposite gate of the Lord’s house, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
This is the living creature I had seen beneath the God of Israel at the river Chebar, and I knew that it was cherubim.
Each had four faces, each had eight wings, and the likeness of human hands was beneath their wings.
As for the likeness of their faces, these are the faces I had seen beneath the glory of the God of Israel at the river Chebar; each of them went straight ahead.

A spirit lifted me and brought me to the opposite gate of the Lord’s house, facing east. And behold, at the gate entrance were about twenty-five men. Among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Ezer and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.
The Lord said to me, “Son of man, these are the men who devise vain things and counsel wicked counsel in this city,
who say, ‘Have the houses not been built recently? She is the cauldron, and we are the meat.’
Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man.”
The Lord’s spirit fell upon me, and He said to me, “Say, ‘Thus says the Lord: You have said this, house of Israel, and I understand the deliberations of your spirit.
You have multiplied your dead in this city and filled her roads with the wounded.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Your dead whom you struck within her are the meat, and she is the cauldron; but I will bring you out of her.
You fear the sword, and I will bring a sword upon you, says the Lord.
I will bring you out of her midst, hand you into foreigners’ hands, and execute judgments among you.
You will fall by the sword. At Israel’s borders I will judge you, and you will recognize that I am the Lord.
She will not be a cauldron for you, and you certainly will not become meat within her. At Israel’s borders I will judge you,
and you will recognize that I am the Lord.’”
As I prophesied, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. I fall upon my face and cried aloud with a loud voice and said, “Alas, alas, Lord! Thou art bringing Israel’s survivors to a complete end!”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

“Son of man, your brothers and the men of your captivity and the whole house of Israel have been brought to an end. To them Jerusalem’s inhabitants said, ‘Keep far from the Lord; the land has been given to us as an inheritance.’
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will thrust them away into the nations and scatter them through all the earth, and I will be a little sanctuary for them in the countries where they may enter.’
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will receive them from the nations and gather them from the countries where I scattered them, and I will give them the land of Israel.
They will enter there and remove all her abominations and all her lawlessness from her.
I will give them another heart and put a new spirit within them. I will tear the stone heart from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
so that they may walk in My commands, keep My ordinances and carry them out. They will be My people, and I will be their God.
As their heart went toward the heart of their abominations and their lawlessness, I have brought their ways upon their heads, says the Lord.’”
The cherubim raised their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was upon them, above them.
The Lord’s glory rose from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain opposite the city.
A spirit lifted me and brought me into the Chaldeans’ land, to the captives, in a vision by God’s spirit. I rose out of the vision I had seen,
and I spoke to the captives all the Lord’s words that He had shown me.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, you dwell in the midst of their injustices. They have eyes to see and do not see, and ears to hear and do not hear, because they are an embittering house.

And you, son of man, get your belongings ready for captivity by day before them. You will be taken captive from your place to another place before them, so that they may see, because they are an embittering house.
You will bring your belongings out like belongings for captivity by day before their eyes, and you yourself will go out in the evening as a captive goes out.
Before them, dig for yourself through the wall, and you will pass out through it.
Before them you will be lifted upon shoulders and go out concealed. Cover your face, and you certainly will not see the land, for I have made you a portent to the house of Israel.”

I did so according to all that He commanded me. I brought belongings out like belongings for captivity by day; in the evening I dug through the wall for myself and went out concealed. I was lifted upon shoulders before them.
In the morning the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, has not the house of Israel, the embittering house, said to you, ‘What are you doing?’
Say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: The ruler and the leader in Jerusalem and in the whole house of Israel, who are among them—’
Say, ‘I perform portents in her midst. As I have done, so it will be for them; in deportation and captivity they will go.’

The ruler among them will be lifted upon shoulders and go out concealed through the wall. He will dig through it to go out through it. He will cover his face so that he may not be seen by an eye, and he himself will not see the land.
I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My enclosure. I will bring him to Babylon, to the Chaldeans’ land, and he will not see it, and there he will die.
All those around him, his helpers and all who support him, I will scatter to every wind; I will draw a sword after them.
They will know that I am the Lord when I scatter them among the nations, and I will disperse them among the countries.
I will spare a few men among them from sword, famine and death, so that they may recount all their lawlessness among the nations where they entered, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, eat your bread with pain, and drink your water with torment and distress,

and say to the people of the land, ‘Thus says the Lord to Jerusalem’s inhabitants upon Israel’s land: They will eat their bread with want and drink their water with devastation, so that the land may be destroyed with its fullness, for all who dwell in it are in impiety.
Their inhabited cities will be made desolate, and the land will be laid waste. You will recognize that I am the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, what is this proverb you have concerning Israel’s land, saying, ‘The days are far off; vision has perished’?

Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will turn back this proverb, and the house of Israel certainly will no longer say this proverb.’ For you will speak to them: ‘The days have drawn near, and the word of every vision,
because there will no longer be any false vision or anyone divining pleasing things among the sons of Israel,
because I, the Lord, will speak My words; I will speak and act, and I certainly will delay no longer. For in your days, embittering house, I will speak a word and act, says the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, behold, the embittering house of Israel keeps saying, ‘The vision this man sees is for many days ahead; this man prophesies of times far ahead.’
Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: None of My words that I may speak will be prolonged any longer. I will speak and act, says the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, prophesy against Israel’s prophets; you will prophesy and say to them, ‘Hear the Lord’s word!
Thus says the Lord: Woe to those who prophesy from their own heart and see nothing at all!
Your prophets, Israel, are like foxes in the wildernesses.
They did not stand in a firm position, and they gathered flocks against the house of Israel. Those saying, ‘On the Lord’s day,’ did not rise.
They see false things and divine vain things, those who say, ‘The Lord says,’ although the Lord has not sent them; and they began to establish a word.
Have you not seen a false vision and spoken vain divinations?
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because your words are false and your divinations vain, therefore behold, I am against you, says the Lord,

and I will stretch out My hand against the prophets who see false things and utter vain things. They will not belong to My people’s instruction, nor be written in the register of the house of Israel, nor enter Israel’s land. They will know that I am the Lord.
Because they misled My people, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there was no peace, and this one builds a wall, and they coat it—if it is going to fall,

say to those coating it, ‘It will fall.’ There will be a flooding downpour, and I will put stones for hurling into their bonds, and they will fall; there will be an upending wind, and it will be split.
And behold, the wall has fallen! Will they not say to you, ‘Where is your coating with which you coated it?’
Therefore thus says the Lord: I will unleash an upending blast with wrath; a flooding downpour will come in My anger, and I will bring the projectile stones in wrath for complete destruction,

and I will tear down the wall you coated, and it will fall. I will lay it upon the ground; its foundations will be uncovered, and it will fall, and you will be brought to an end with rebukes. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
I will complete My wrath upon the wall and those coating it, and it will fall. I said to you, ‘There is no wall, nor those coating it—
the prophets of Israel who prophesy concerning Jerusalem and see peace for her, when there is no peace,’ says the Lord.’
And you, son of man, set your face firmly against the daughters of your people who prophesy from their own heart, and prophesy against them,

and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Woe to the women sewing cushions upon every elbow of an arm and making coverings upon every head of every age, to distort lives! The lives of My people were distorted, and they were preserving lives.

They were profaning Me among My people for a handful of barley and scraps of bread, putting to death lives that ought not die and preserving lives that ought not live, as you uttered things to a people listening to vain pronouncements.

Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against your cushions, on which you entangle lives. I will tear them from your arms and send the lives out—their lives that you twist away—into dispersion.
I will tear your coverings and rescue My people from your hand. They will no longer be in your hands for entanglement, and you will recognize that I am the Lord.
Because you distorted the righteous person’s heart unjustly, though I was not distorting him, and strengthened the lawless person’s hands so that he does not turn at all from his evil way and live,
therefore you certainly will no longer see false things or divine divinations. I will rescue My people from your hand, and you will know that I am the Lord.’”
Men from Israel’s elders came to me and sat before me.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, these men have set their thoughts upon their hearts and set the punishment of their injustices before their faces. Shall I indeed answer them?

Therefore speak to them and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: Anyone of the house of Israel who sets his thoughts upon his heart, places the punishment of his injustice before his face, and comes to the prophet—I, the Lord, will answer him in the things in which his mind is entangled,
so that it may turn the house of Israel aside in accordance with their hearts, alienated from Me through their reflections.’
Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Turn back and turn away from your practices and all your impieties, and turn your faces.

For anyone of the house of Israel or of the sojourners living among Israel who becomes alienated from Me, sets his reflections upon his heart, places the punishment of his injustice before his face, and comes to the prophet to question him concerning Me—I, the Lord, will answer him in that in which he is entangled.
I will set My face firmly against that person, make him a wilderness and a devastation, and remove him from the midst of My people. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
If the prophet is led astray and speaks, I, the Lord, have led that prophet astray. I will stretch out My hand against him and destroy him from the midst of My people Israel.
They will receive their injustice; according to the inquirer’s offense and according to the offense, it will likewise be for the prophet,
so that the house of Israel may no longer wander from Me or be defiled by any of their transgressions. They will be My people, and I will be their God, says the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, if a land sins against Me by committing a transgression, and I stretch My hand against it, shatter its support of bread, send famine upon it, and remove human and livestock from it,
even if these three men—Noah, Daniel and Job—were within it, they themselves would be saved by their righteousness, says the Lord.
Even if I bring evil beasts upon the land and punish it, so that it becomes a devastation and no one passes through because of the beasts,
and these three men were within it, as I live, says the Lord, neither sons nor daughters would be saved; only they themselves would be saved, and the land would be destroyed.
Or even if I bring a sword upon that land and say, ‘Let a sword pass through the land,’ and remove human and livestock from it,
and these three men were within it, as I live, says the Lord, they certainly would not rescue sons or daughters; they alone would be saved.
Or even if I send death upon that land and pour My wrath upon it in blood, to destroy human and livestock from it,
and Noah, Daniel and Job were within it, as I live, says the Lord, neither sons nor daughters would be left; they would rescue their own lives by their righteousness.
Thus says the Lord: Even if I send My four evil retributions—sword, famine, evil beasts and death—against Jerusalem, to destroy human and livestock from her,

and behold, her rescued survivors are left in her, bringing sons and daughters out of her. Behold, they are coming out to you. You will see their ways and their reflections and feel regret over the evils I brought upon Jerusalem—all the evils I brought upon her,
and they will comfort you, because you will see their ways and their reflections, and recognize that I have not done in vain all that I did in her, says the Lord.”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“And you, son of man, what could vinewood be among all the branch wood found among the forest trees?
Will they take wood from it to make anything useful? Will they take a peg from it to hang any vessel upon it?
It has only been given to the fire to be consumed. Fire consumes its yearly prunings, and it is utterly spent. Surely it will not be useful for work?
Even when it is whole, it will not serve for work. How much less if fire consumes it completely—will it still serve for work?
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: As with the vinewood among the forest trees, which I have given to the fire to be consumed, so I have given Jerusalem’s inhabitants.
I will set My face against them. They will come out of the fire, and fire will devour them. They will recognize that I am the Lord when I set My face firmly against them.
I will lay the land waste, because they have fallen into transgression, says the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, solemnly testify to Jerusalem about her lawlessness,
and say, ‘Thus says the Lord to Jerusalem: Your root and your birth are from the land of Canaan; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.
As for your birth, on the day you were born they did not bind your breasts; you were not washed with water, not salted with salt, and not wrapped in swaddling cloths.
Nor did My eye spare you to do any of all these things for you, to feel anything for you. You were cast upon the face of the plain because of your life’s crookedness, on the day you were born.
I passed by you and saw you befouled in your blood, and said to you, ‘From your blood, life!
Multiply!’ I have made you like the growth of the field. You multiplied, grew great and entered cities of cities. Your breasts stood firm and your hair grew, but you were naked and exposed.

I passed through you and saw you; behold, your season was the season of those lodging. I spread My wings over you and covered your exposure. I swore to you and entered a covenant with you, says the Lord, and you became Mine.
I washed you with water, washed your blood off you, and anointed you with oil,
and clothed you in patterned garments, gave you blue-purple footwear, girded you with fine linen, and wrapped you in hair-woven cloth,
and adorned you with ornaments, placed bracelets around your hands and a necklace around your neck,
and put a ring around your nostril, little hoops upon your ears and a crown of boasting upon your head.
You were adorned with gold and silver; your coverings were fine linen, hair-woven and patterned. You ate fine flour, oil and honey, and became very beautiful.
Your fame went out among the nations because of your beauty, for it was made complete in splendor, in the loveliness I placed upon you, says the Lord.
You trusted in your beauty and prostituted yourself because of your fame. You poured out your prostitution upon every passerby—which will not be.
You took some of your garments, made sewn idols for yourself and prostituted yourself upon them. You certainly will not enter, nor will it come to be.
You took your vessels of boasting from My gold and My silver, from what I had given you, made male images for yourself and prostituted yourself among them.
You took your patterned clothing and clothed them; you set My oil and My incense before them.
My loaves that I gave you—fine flour, oil and honey with which I fed you—you set before them as a fragrant aroma. So it happened, says the Lord.
You took your sons and daughters whom you had borne and sacrificed them to them for consumption, as though you had prostituted yourself only a little,
and slaughtered your children and gave them over as you used them for averting rites.
This was in addition to all your prostitution, and you did not remember the days of your infancy, when you were naked and exposed and lived befouled in your blood.
After all your evils, says the Lord,
you built yourself a prostitution chamber and made yourself a display place in every broad street,
and at the head of every road you built your brothels, ruined your beauty, spread your legs to every passerby, and multiplied your prostitution.
You prostituted yourself with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors great in flesh, and prostituted yourself in many ways to anger Me.

But if I stretch My hand against you, I will remove your ordinances and hand you over to the desires of those who hate you, daughters of foreigners who turn you aside from your way in which you acted impiously.
You prostituted yourself with the daughters of Assyria, and not even so were you filled; you prostituted yourself, and were not filled.
You multiplied your covenants toward the Chaldeans’ land, and not even with these were you filled.
What shall I do to your daughter, says the Lord, when you do all these things, the works of a prostitute? And you prostituted yourself threefold
among your daughters. You built your brothel at every road head and made your platform in every broad street, and became like a prostitute gathering payments.
The adulterous wife is like you, receiving payments from her husband;
she kept giving payments to all who prostituted her. You too gave payments to all your lovers and loaded them up to come to you from all around in your prostitution.

With you it became distorted compared with other women in your prostitution. They have prostituted themselves with you as you paid extra payments, and no payments were given to you; with you things became distorted.
Therefore, prostitute, hear the Lord’s word!

Thus says the Lord: Because you poured out your copper, your shame will be exposed in your prostitution with your lovers, in all the reflections of your lawlessness, and in the blood of your children whom you gave to them.

Therefore behold, I am gathering against you all your lovers with whom you mingled, all whom you loved together with all whom you hated. I will gather them against you from all around, reveal your evils to them, and they will see all your shame.
I will exact retribution upon you with the retribution of an adulteress and a woman shedding blood, and place you in blood of wrath and jealousy.
I will hand you into their hands. They will tear down your brothel, pull down your platform, strip your clothing from you, take your vessels of boasting, and leave you naked and exposed.
They will bring crowds against you, stone you with stones, and slaughter you with their swords.
They will burn your houses with fire and exact retributions upon you before many women. I will turn you away from your prostitution, and you certainly will give no more payments.
I will release My wrath upon you; My jealousy will be removed from you. I will rest and certainly be concerned no longer.

Because you did not remember the day of your infancy but grieved Me with all these things, behold, I have brought your ways upon your head, says the Lord. Thus you committed impiety in addition to all your lawlessness.
These are all the things they said against you in a proverb, saying, ‘As the mother, so the daughter.’

You are the daughter of your mother, who rejected her husband and her children, and the sister of your sisters, who rejected their husbands and children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
Your elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters, dwelling at your left; your sister younger than you, dwelling at your right, is Sodom and her daughters.
Not even so did you walk in their ways or act according to their lawlessness. Before long, you surpass them in all your ways.
As I live, says the Lord, your sister Sodom, she and her daughters, certainly did not do as you and your daughters have done.

Yet this was the lawlessness of your sister Sodom: arrogance. In fullness of bread and abundance of wine she and her daughters lived luxuriously. This belonged to her and her daughters, but they did not support the hand of the poor and needy.
They boasted greatly and committed acts of lawlessness before Me, and I removed them as I saw.
Samaria did not sin half your sins. You multiplied your lawlessness beyond theirs and justified your sisters by all the lawlessness you committed.

You too, receive your torment, in which you corrupted your sisters by your sins, in which you acted more lawlessly than they and justified them above yourself. You too, be ashamed and take your dishonor, in that you justified your sisters.
I will reverse their reversals—the reversal of Sodom and her daughters; I will reverse the reversal of Samaria and her daughters; and I will reverse your reversal among them,
so that you may receive your torment and be dishonored for all you did in provoking Me.

Your sister Sodom and her daughters will be restored as they were from the beginning; Samaria and her daughters will be restored as they were from the beginning; and you and your daughters will be restored as you were from the beginning.
And if your sister Sodom was not a report in your mouth in the days of your arrogance,
before your evils were revealed—as now you are a reproach of Syria’s daughters and all around her, daughters of foreigners who surround you all around?
Your impieties and your lawlessness—you have borne them, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: I will deal with you as you have done, as you dishonored these things by transgressing My covenant.
I Myself will remember My covenant with you in the days of your infancy and raise up for you an eternal covenant.

You will remember your way and be dishonored when you take up your sisters, those older than you together with those younger than you. I will give them to you for building up, and not from your covenant.
I Myself will raise up My covenant with you, and you will recognize that I am the Lord,
so that you may remember and be ashamed, and no longer have occasion to open your mouth because of your dishonor, when I am propitious to you concerning all that you have done, says the Lord.’”
And it happened in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth of the month, while I was among the captives by the River Chebar: the heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.
On the fifth of the month—this was the fifth year of King Jehoiakim’s captivity—
the Lord’s word came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the River Chebar; and the Lord’s hand came upon me,

and I looked, and behold, a sweeping wind was coming from the north, and a great cloud was within it, with brightness around it and fire flashing like lightning; within it was something like the appearance of electrum, within the fire, and brightness within it.
And within it was something like a likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: a human likeness was upon them,
and each had four faces, and each had four wings.
Their legs were straight, and their feet were winged, with sparks like flashing bronze; and their wings were light.
A human hand was beneath their wings on their four sides; and the faces of all four of them
did not turn as they walked; each went straight ahead.
The likeness of their faces was a human face and a lion’s face on the right for all four, and a calf’s face on the left for all four, and an eagle’s face for all four.
The wings of all four were stretched out above; each had two joined to one another, and two covered the top of their bodies.
Each went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit was going, they went and did not turn.
And amid the living creatures was an appearance like burning coals of fire, like the sight of torches whirling among the living creatures, and brightness of the fire; lightning came out of the fire.
I looked, and behold, one wheel was on the earth adjoining the four living creatures;
the appearance of the wheels was like the appearance of tharsis, and all four had one likeness; their workmanship was as though a wheel were within a wheel.
They went toward their four sides; they did not turn as they went,
nor did their backs; they were tall, and I saw them. The backs of all four were full of eyes all around.
When the living creatures went, the wheels moved beside them; when the living creatures rose from the earth, the wheels rose.
Wherever the cloud was, there was the spirit for movement; the living creatures and the wheels went and rose together with them, because a spirit of life was in the wheels.
When they went, these went; when they stood, these stood; when they rose from the earth, these rose together with them, because a spirit of life was in the wheels.
Above the living creatures’ heads was a likeness as of a firmament, like the appearance of crystal, stretched out above their wings;
and beneath the firmament their wings were stretched out, fluttering one toward another; each had two joined together, covering their bodies.
As they went, I heard the sound of their wings like the sound of much water; when they stood, their wings came to rest.
And behold, a voice came from above the firmament that was over their heads.
Like the appearance of a sapphire stone was the likeness of a throne upon it; and above the likeness of the throne was a likeness like the form of a human being.

I saw something like the sight of electrum from the appearance of a waist upward; and from the appearance of a waist down below I saw something like the appearance of fire, with its brightness all around.

Like the appearance of a bow when it is in the cloud on a rainy day, so was the arrangement of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of the Lord’s glory. I saw it, and I fall upon my face, and I heard the voice of One speaking.
He said to me, “Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak to you.”
A spirit came upon me, took me up, raised me, and set me on my feet; I heard Him speaking to me,
and He said to me, “Son of man, I am sending you out to the house of Israel, those who embitter Me, who have embittered Me, they and their fathers, until this present day,
and you will say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord.’
If indeed they listen or are terrified—for it is an embittering house—they will know that you are a prophet among them.

And you, son of man, do not fear them or be shaken before their faces, because they will rage and gather against you all around, and you dwell among scorpions. Do not fear their words or be shaken before their faces, for it is an embittering house.
You will speak My words to them, if indeed they listen or are terrified, for it is an embittering house.
And you, son of man, hear the One speaking to you. Do not become embittering like the embittering house. Open your mouth wide and eat what I give you.”
I looked, and behold, a hand was stretched toward me, and in it was a scroll of a book;
and He unrolled it before me. It had writing on the back and the front, and upon it were written a lament, a song and woe.
He said to me, “Son of man, eat this scroll, then go and speak to the sons of Israel.”
I opened my mouth wide, and He fed me the scroll.
He said to me, “Son of man, your mouth will eat, and your belly will be filled with this scroll that has been given to you.” I ate it, and in my mouth it became like sweet honey.
He said to me, “Son of man, go, enter the house of Israel, and speak My words to them;
for you are not sent out to a people of deep speech and heavy tongue, but to the house of Israel,
nor to many peoples of foreign speech or foreign tongues, nor those strong in tongue whose words you will not understand. If I had sent you to such people, they would have listened to you.
But the house of Israel certainly will not be willing to listen to you, because they do not wish to listen to Me; the entire house of Israel is contentious and hard-hearted.
Behold, I have made your face strong against their faces, and I will strengthen your contention against their contention,
and it will always be stronger than rock. Do not fear them or be terrified before their faces, for it is an embittering house.”
He said to me, “Son of man, take into your heart all the words that I have spoken with you, and hear with your ears,
and go, enter the captivity, to the sons of your people; you will speak to them and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord,’ if indeed they listen, if indeed they yield.”
A spirit took me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great shaking: “Blessed be the Lord’s glory from His place!”
I saw the sound of the living creatures’ wings fluttering one toward another, and the sound of the wheels adjoining them, and the sound of the shaking.
The spirit raised me and took me up. I went, impelled by my spirit, and the Lord’s hand came strongly upon me.
I entered the captivity aloft and went around those dwelling by the River Chebar, those who were there; I sat there seven days, living among them.
After the seven days, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for the house of Israel. You will hear a word from My mouth and convey My warning to them.

When I say to the lawless person, ‘You will surely be put to death,’ and you do not warn him or speak to warn the lawless person to turn from his ways so that he may live, that lawless person will die in his injustice; but I will require his blood from your hand.
But if you warn the lawless person and he does not turn from his lawlessness and his way, that lawless person will die in his injustice, while you will rescue your life.

When a righteous person turns from his righteous deeds and commits a transgression, and I place torment before his face, he will die because you did not warn him. He will die in his sins, because the righteous deeds he did certainly will not be remembered, and I will require his blood from your hand.
But if you warn the righteous person not to sin, and he does not sin, the righteous person will surely live because you warned him; and you will rescue your own life.”
The Lord’s hand came upon me, and He said to me, “Rise and go out to the plain, and you will be spoken to there.”
I rose and went out to the plain, and behold, the Lord’s glory stood there, like the vision and like the glory I had seen by the River Chebar; and I fall upon my face.
A spirit came upon me and set me on my feet. He spoke to me and said to me, “Go, be shut inside your house.
And you, son of man, behold, bonds have been placed upon you, and they will bind you with them; you certainly will not go out from among them.
I will bind your tongue, and you will become mute; you will not be a man rebuking them, for it is an embittering house.
But when I speak to you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: Let the one who hears hear, and let the one who disobeys disobey,’ for it is an embittering house.”
“And you, son of man, take a brick, set it before your face, and draw upon it a city—Jerusalem;
lay siege to it, build forward defenses against it, throw up a palisade against it, set camps against it, and arrange missile positions all around.
Take an iron pan and place it as an iron wall between you and the city. Prepare your face against it; it will be besieged, and you will besiege it. This is a sign for the sons of Israel.
Lie on your left side and place the injustices of the house of Israel upon it, according to the number of days—one hundred fifty—that you lie upon it; bear their injustices.
I have assigned you their two injustices as a number of days, one hundred ninety days; bear the injustices of the house of Israel
and complete all these things. Lie on your right side and bear the injustices of the house of Judah forty days. I have appointed you a day for a year.
Prepare your face against Jerusalem’s siege, strengthen your arm, and prophesy against it.
Behold, I have placed bonds upon you; do not turn from side to side until the days of your confinement are completed.

Take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet and spelt; put them in one earthen vessel and make loaves from them for yourself. According to the number of days you sleep on your side, you will eat them one hundred ninety days.
The food you are to eat will be weighed out: twenty shekels a day; eat it from time to time.
Drink water by measure, the sixth part of a hin; drink it from time to time.
Eat it as a barley cake baked in embers; bake it in pellets of human dung before their eyes,
and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: So the sons of Israel will eat unclean things among the nations.’”

I said, “By no means, Lord, God of Israel! Behold, my life has not been defiled with uncleanness. From my birth until now I have eaten neither what died of itself nor what a wild animal killed, nor has any stale meat entered my mouth.”
He said to me, “Behold, I have given you cattle dung instead of human dung; prepare your loaves over it.”
He said to me, “Son of man, behold, I am breaking the support of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight and in need, and drink water by measure and in devastation,
so that they become needy for bread and water. A man and his brother will disappear, and they will waste away in their injustices.
“And you, son of man, take a sword sharper than a barber’s razor. Obtain it for yourself and pass it over your head and your beard. Take a balance with weights and divide the hairs;

burn a quarter with fire inside the city when the days of siege are complete. Take a quarter and burn it up in its midst; cut down a quarter with the sword around it, and scatter a quarter to the wind. I will draw a sword after them.
Take a few of them in number and gather them into your cloak.
Take some of these again, cast them into the fire, and burn them in the fire. From it fire will go out. And you will say to the entire house of Israel,
‘Thus says the Lord: This is Jerusalem. I have placed her amid the nations, and the lands around her.
And you will speak My ordinances to the lawless one among the nations, and My laws among the lands around her; for they rejected My ordinances and did not walk in My laws.

Therefore thus says the Lord: Because your impulse comes from the nations around you, and you have not walked in My laws or performed My ordinances—nor have you even acted according to the ordinances of the nations around you—
therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against you, and I will execute judgment in your midst before the nations,
and I will do among you what I have not done and the like of which I will not do again, according to all your abominations.
Therefore fathers will eat children in your midst, and children will eat fathers. I will execute judgments against you and scatter all your survivors to every wind.
Therefore, as I live, says the Lord, surely, because you defiled My holy places with all your abominations, I too will reject you. My eye will not spare, and I too will have no mercy.

A quarter of you will be consumed by death; a quarter of you will perish by famine within you; a quarter of you I will scatter to every wind; and a quarter of you will fall by the sword around you, and I will draw a sword after them.
My wrath and My anger against them will be completed, and you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken in My jealousy when I complete My anger against them.
I will make you a wilderness, and your daughters around you, before every passerby;
you will be mourned and ravaged among the nations around you when I execute judgments against you in the vengeance of My wrath. I, the Lord, have spoken.
When I send My arrows of famine against them, they will bring exhaustion, and I will break your support of bread.
I will send famine and harmful wild animals against you, and I will punish you. Death and blood will pass over you, and I will bring a sword upon you all around. I, the Lord, have spoken.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, set your face firmly against the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them,

and say, ‘Mountains of Israel, hear the Lord’s word. Thus says the Lord to the mountains, hills, ravines and wooded valleys: Behold, I am bringing a sword against you, and your high places will be destroyed,
and your altars and your sacred precincts will be shattered; I will cast down your wounded before your idols,
and I will scatter your bones around your altars.
In all your dwelling territory the cities will be made desolate and the high places will disappear, so that your altars are destroyed, your idols shattered, and your sacred precincts removed;
wounded people will fall in your midst, and you will recognize that I am the Lord.
When there are among you survivors of the sword among the nations, and in your scattering in the lands,

the survivors from among you will remember Me among the nations where they were taken captive. I have sworn against their heart that whores away from Me and their eyes that whore after their pursuits; they will beat their faces over all their abominations.
They will recognize that I, the Lord, have spoken.
Thus says the Lord: Clap your hand, stamp your foot, and say, “Aha! Aha!” over all the abominations of the house of Israel; they will fall by sword, death and famine.
The one near will fall by the sword, the one far away will die by death, and the one enclosed will perish by famine; I will complete My anger against them.
You will know that I am the Lord when your wounded lie among your idols, around your altars, on every high hill and beneath a shady tree, where they offered a fragrant aroma to all their idols.
I will stretch out My hand against them and reduce the land to ruin and destruction, from the wilderness of Deblatha, from every dwelling place; you will recognize that I am the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“And you, son of man, say, ‘Thus says the Lord to the land of Israel: An end has come; the end has come upon the four wings of the land.
The end has come
upon you, inhabitant of the land. The time has come; the day has drawn near, neither with tumult nor with birth pangs.
Now soon I will pour My anger upon you and complete My wrath in you; I will judge you in your ways and bring all your abominations upon you.
My eye will not spare, nor will I have mercy; I will bring your ways upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. You will recognize that I am the Lord who strikes.
Now the end is upon you. I Myself will send against you and exact retribution upon you in your ways; I will bring all your abominations upon you.
My eye will not spare you, nor will I have mercy; I will bring your way upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
For thus says the Lord:
Behold, the end has come; behold, the Lord’s day! Even if the rod has blossomed, insolence has risen.
It will shatter the support of a lawless person, neither with tumult nor with haste.
The time has come; behold, the day! Let the buyer not rejoice, nor the seller lament;
for the buyer certainly will no longer return to the seller, and a person will not prevail in the eye of his life.
Sound the trumpet and judge everything.
War by the sword is outside, and famine and death inside. The one in the plain will die by the sword, while famine and death will consume those in the city.
Their survivors will be saved and be on the mountains; I will kill them all, each in his injustices.
All hands will weaken, and all thighs will be defiled with moisture,
and they will gird on sackcloth; amazement will cover them, shame will be upon every face among them, and baldness upon every head.

Their silver will be thrown into the broad streets, and their gold will be disregarded. Their lives certainly will not be satisfied, nor their bellies filled, because it became torment for their injustices.
They made choice ornaments a source of arrogance and made images of their abominations from them. Therefore I have given them over to them as uncleanness.
I will hand them into foreigners’ hands to plunder them, and to the pestilent people of the earth as spoils; they will profane them.
I will turn My face away from them, and they will defile My oversight; they will enter them unguarded and profane them,
and they will make a confused mixture, because the land is full of peoples and the city full of lawlessness.
I will turn back the arrogance of their strength, and their holy places will be defiled.
Propitiation will come and will seek peace, and there will be none.
Woe upon woe will come, and message upon message; a vision will be sought from a prophet, but law will perish from a priest and counsel from elders.

A ruler will clothe himself in devastation, and the hands of the people of the land will be paralyzed. According to their ways I will deal with them, and by their judgments I will exact retribution upon them; they will know that I am the Lord.’”
In the sixth year, in the fifth month, on the fifth of the month, I was sitting in the house, and Judah’s elders were sitting before me. The Lord’s hand came upon me,
and I saw, and behold, the likeness of a man: from His waist downward, fire, and from His waist upward, like the appearance of electrum.

He stretched out the likeness of a hand and lifted me by the crown of my head. A spirit lifted me between earth and heaven and brought me to Jerusalem in a vision of God, to the entrance of the inner gate facing north, where the pillar of the one acquiring stood.
And behold, the glory of the Lord God of Israel was there, in accordance with the vision I had seen in the plain.
He said to me, “Son of man, look up with your eyes toward the north.” I looked up with my eyes toward the north, and behold, from the north to the gate toward the east.
He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what these people do? They commit great lawlessness here, to keep away from My holy places. You will yet see greater lawlessness.”
He brought me to the courtyard entrance
and said to me, “Son of man, dig.” I dug, and behold, there was a door.
He said to me, “Go in and see the lawlessness these people are committing here.”
I went in and saw, and behold, vain abominations and all the idols of the house of Israel were drawn upon it all around,
and there were seventy men from the elders of the house of Israel. Jaazaniah son of Shaphan stood among them before their faces; each had his censer in his hand, and the vapor of incense rose.
He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel do, each in their hidden bedchamber? For they said, ‘The Lord does not see; the Lord has abandoned the land.’”
He said to me, “You will yet see greater lawlessness that these people are committing.”
He brought me to the entrance of the gate of the Lord’s house facing north, and behold, women were sitting there lamenting Tammuz,
and He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen? You will yet see practices greater than these.”

He brought me into the inner court of the Lord’s house, and behold, at the entrance of the Lord’s temple, between the porches and the altar, were about twenty men, their backs toward the Lord’s temple and their faces opposite. These were bowing to the sun.

He said to me, “Have you seen, son of man? Is it a small thing for the house of Judah to commit the lawlessness they have committed here? For they have filled the land with lawlessness, and behold, they are as though sneering.
I too will act toward them in wrath. My eye will not spare, nor will I have mercy.”

units.text: David assembled in Jerusalem all Israel’s rulers: the rulers of the judges, the rulers of the service courses attending the king’s person, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the treasury keepers, those over his possessions, the powerful men, and the army’s warriors.
See, therefore, that the Lord has chosen you to build Him a house as a sanctuary. Be strong and act.”

David stood in the midst of the assembly and said, “Hear me, brethren and my people. It came upon my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the Lord’s covenant and a standing place for our Lord’s feet, and I prepared the things suitable for the dwelling.
But God said, ‘You shall not build Me a house to have My name called upon it, because you are a warrior and have shed blood.’

Now, before the whole assembly of the Lord and in the ears of our God, observe and seek all the commandments of the Lord our God, so that you may inherit the good land and pass it on as an inheritance to your sons after you for ever.

And now, Solomon my son, know the God of your fathers, and serve Him with a whole heart and a willing soul; for the Lord examines every heart and knows every thought. If you seek Him, He shall be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you utterly.
Micaiah said, “Not so—not I! Hear the Lord’s word—not so! I saw the Lord, the God of Israel, sitting on His throne, and all the army of heaven stood around Him, on His right and His left.
The Lord said, ‘Who will deceive Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Remmath-gilead?’ One said this, and another said that.
A spirit came forward, stood before the Lord, and said, ‘I will deceive him.’ The Lord said to it, ‘By what means?’
It said, ‘I will go out and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’ He said, ‘You will deceive him and indeed prevail. Go out and do so.’
Now behold, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken calamities against you.”
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah approached, struck Micaiah on the cheek, and said, “What sort of spirit of the Lord was it that spoke in you?”

When Solomon had finished building the Lord’s house and his own house after twenty years, King Solomon assembled all Israel’s elders in Zion to bring up the ark of the Lord’s covenant from the City of David, which is Zion,
When the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house.
The priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the Lord’s glory filled the house.
The king turned his face, and the king blessed all Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood.
in the month of Athanin.
The priests carried the ark
and the tent of testimony and all the holy utensils in the tent of testimony,
The king and all the sons of Israel offered a sacrifice before the Lord.

King Solomon offered the peace offerings that he sacrificed to the Lord: twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred twenty thousand sheep. Thus the king and all the sons of Israel dedicated the Lord’s house.

There was nothing in the ark except two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant, which Moses had placed there at Horeb, when the Lord made a covenant with the sons of Israel as they came out of the land of Egypt.

But if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in this matter.
For it is time for judgment to begin from the house of God; and if it begins first from us, what will be the outcome for those who disobey the good news of God?
