Nabouzardan, the chief cook, removed the rest of the people left in the city, those who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the remaining support.
The chief cook left some of the land’s poor as vinedressers and as gabin.
In the fifth month, on the seventh of the month, in the nineteenth year of Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon, Nabouzardan, the chief cook who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
He set fire to the Lord’s house, the king’s house, and all Jerusalem’s houses; every house was set ablaze by
Simeon Peter, a slave and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have received a faith of equal honor with ours through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ:
so that you may remember the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets and the commandment of the Lord and Savior through your apostles,
knowing this first: in the last days scoffers will come with scoffing, walking according to their own desires,
and saying, “Where is the promise of His coming? For ever since the fathers fell asleep, everything continues as it was from the beginning of creation.”
For they willingly overlook this: that heavens existed long ago, and earth was formed out of water and through water by the word of God,
Woe to those desiring the Lord’s day! Why is this Lord’s day for you? It is darkness, not light,
as when someone flees from a lion and a bear falls upon him, then leaps into his house, braces his hands upon the wall, and a snake bites him.
Is not the Lord’s day darkness rather than light, gloom that has no brightness in it?

all of you cross over and see; pass from there to Emath Rabba, and go down from there to Geth of foreigners, the strongest of all these kingdoms, to see whether their borders are greater than your borders.
You come toward an evil day, drawing near and touching false sabbaths,
sleeping upon ivory beds and indulging upon your couches, eating young goats from the flocks and milk-fed calves from the herds,
clapping to the sound of instruments; they reckoned them as lasting, not passing away,
drinking strained wine and anointing yourselves with the finest perfumes, yet suffering nothing over Joseph’s shattering.
Therefore now they will be captives from the foremost of the powerful, and horses’ neighing will be removed from Ephraim.
Then the king returned to his royal residence and spent the night fasting, grieving over Daniel. Daniel’s God, taking care of him, shut the lions’ mouths, and they did not trouble Daniel.
King Darius rose early in the morning, took the satraps with him, and went and stood at the mouth of the lions’ pit.

Then the king called to Daniel with a loud voice and weeping: “O Daniel, are you perhaps alive? Has your God, whom you worship continually, saved you from the lions, so that they have not destroyed you?”
Then Daniel answered with a loud voice and said, “O king, I am still alive,

and God has saved me from the lions, because righteousness was found in me before Him. Before you also, O king, neither ignorant fault nor sin was found in me. Yet you listened to men who mislead kings and threw me into the lions’ pit for destruction.”
Then all the forces assembled and saw Daniel, whom the lions had not troubled.
Then those two men who had testified against Daniel, with their wives and children, were thrown to the lions. The lions killed them and crushed their bones.
Then Darius wrote to all nations, countries, and languages dwelling throughout his whole land, saying:
“Let all people in my kingdom bow to and worship Daniel’s God, for He is God who endures and lives from generation to generation for ever.
I, Darius, will bow to Him and serve Him all my days, for handmade idols cannot save as Daniel’s God redeemed Daniel.”
King Darius was gathered to his people, and Daniel was appointed in Darius’s reign. Cyrus the Persian received his kingdom.
and all the nations shall say, Why has the Lord done thus unto this land? What does this great heat of anger mean?
And they shall say, Because they forsook the covenant of the Lord, the God of their fathers, which He made with their fathers when He brought them forth out of the land of Egypt;
and they went and served other gods, and bowed down unto them, whom they did not know, and whom He had not allotted unto them.
And the Lord was kindled in wrath against that land, to bring upon it all the curses which are written in this book of the law.
And the Lord removed them from their land in wrath, and anger, and exceeding great indignation, and cast them into another land, as it is now.
The hidden things belong unto the Lord our God; but the things revealed belong unto us and unto our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.

And it shall be, when all these things come upon you, the blessing and the curse which I have set before your face, and you receive them into your heart among all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you,
And Moses spoke in the hearing of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song, even unto the end:
He sustained him in a wilderness land, in the thirst of burning heat, in a waterless place; He compassed him about, and instructed him, and kept him as the pupil of an eye.
As an eagle would shelter its nest, it yearned over its young; spreading its wings, it received them, and took them up upon its back.
The Lord alone led them, and there was no foreign god with them.
He brought them up upon the strength of the earth, and fed them the produce of the fields; they sucked honey out of the rock, and oil out of the solid rock,
butter of cattle and milk of sheep, with the fat of lambs and rams, young bulls and goats, with the fat of the kernels of wheat; and they drank wine, the blood of the grape.
And Jacob ate and was filled, and the beloved one kicked; he grew fat, he grew thick, he grew broad; and he forsook God who made him, and departed from God his Saviour.
They provoked Me with foreign gods; with their abominations they embittered Me.
They sacrificed unto demons, and not unto God, unto gods whom they did not know; new ones, lately come, whom their fathers did not know.
You forsook God who begat you, and forgot God who nourishes you.
And the Lord saw, and was jealous, and was provoked by the anger of His sons and daughters.
And His people Jacob became the portion of the Lord; Israel, the measured lot of His inheritance.
All the commandments which I command you this day you shall take heed to do, that you may live and multiply, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God sware unto your fathers.

And you shall remember all the way wherein the Lord your God led you in the wilderness, to afflict you and to test you, that the things in your heart might be known, whether you would keep His commandments or not.

And He afflicted you, and made you hunger, and fed you with manna, which your fathers did not know, that He might declare unto you that man shall not live by bread alone, but man shall live by every word that proceeds through the mouth of God.
Your garments did not wear out upon you, neither did your feet become calloused; behold, these forty years.
I will go through the land of Egypt that night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal. Against all the Egyptians’ gods I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.
And the blood shall be a sign to you upon the houses in which you are; and I will see the blood, and shelter you; and no plague of destruction shall be among you when I strike the land of Egypt.
This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout all your generations; you shall celebrate it as a perpetual statute.
Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood beside the door, and touch the lintel and both doorposts with the blood beside the door. None of you shall go out of the door of his house until morning.

The Lord will pass through to strike the Egyptians. He will see the blood on the lintel and both doorposts, and the Lord will pass by the doorway. He will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses to strike.
And you shall keep this word as a statute for yourself and for your sons for ever.
And Joseph died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.
And the sons of Israel increased and multiplied, and became numerous and exceedingly, exceedingly strong; and the land multiplied them.
And another king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
I saw, and behold, above the firmament over the cherubim’s head was something like sapphire stone, a throne’s likeness above them.
Their appearance was one likeness for all four, as when a wheel is within a wheel.
As they went, they went toward their four directions; they did not turn as they went. For wherever the one leading part looked, they went, and they did not turn as they went.
Their backs, their hands, their wings, and the wheels were full of eyes all around, upon their four wheels.
These wheels were called “Gelgel” in my hearing.
The cherubim lifted themselves. This was the living creature I had seen at the river Chebar.
When the cherubim went, the wheels went beside them. When the cherubim raised their wings to rise from the earth, their wheels did not turn.
When they stood, these stood; when they rose, these rose with them, because a spirit of life was in them.
The Lord’s glory went out from the house and mounted upon the cherubim,

and the cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the earth before me as they went out, with the wheels beside them. They stood at the entrance of the opposite gate of the Lord’s house, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
He said to the man wearing the robe, “Go in among the wheels beneath the cherubim, fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim, and scatter them over the city.” He went in before me.
This is the living creature I had seen beneath the God of Israel at the river Chebar, and I knew that it was cherubim.
Each had four faces, each had eight wings, and the likeness of human hands was beneath their wings.
As for the likeness of their faces, these are the faces I had seen beneath the glory of the God of Israel at the river Chebar; each of them went straight ahead.
The cherubim stood to the right of the house as the man entered, and the cloud filled the inner court.
The Lord’s glory departed from the cherubim to the forecourt of the house. The cloud filled the house, and the court filled with the radiance of the Lord’s glory.
The sound of the cherubim’s wings was heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Shaddai speaking.
When He commanded the man wearing the holy robe, saying, “Take fire from among the wheels, from among the cherubim,” he entered and stood beside the wheels,
and he stretched out his hand into the midst of the fire among the cherubim, took it and gave it into the hands of the man wearing the holy robe. He took it and went out.
I saw the cherubim, the likeness of human hands beneath their wings.
I saw, and behold, four wheels stood beside the cherubim, one wheel beside one cherub. The wheels’ appearance was like the appearance of a carbuncle stone.

A spirit lifted me and brought me to the opposite gate of the Lord’s house, facing east. And behold, at the gate entrance were about twenty-five men. Among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Ezer and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.
You will fall by the sword. At Israel’s borders I will judge you, and you will recognize that I am the Lord.
She will not be a cauldron for you, and you certainly will not become meat within her. At Israel’s borders I will judge you,
and you will recognize that I am the Lord.’”
As I prophesied, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. I fall upon my face and cried aloud with a loud voice and said, “Alas, alas, Lord! Thou art bringing Israel’s survivors to a complete end!”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

“Son of man, your brothers and the men of your captivity and the whole house of Israel have been brought to an end. To them Jerusalem’s inhabitants said, ‘Keep far from the Lord; the land has been given to us as an inheritance.’
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will thrust them away into the nations and scatter them through all the earth, and I will be a little sanctuary for them in the countries where they may enter.’
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will receive them from the nations and gather them from the countries where I scattered them, and I will give them the land of Israel.
They will enter there and remove all her abominations and all her lawlessness from her.
I will give them another heart and put a new spirit within them. I will tear the stone heart from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
The Lord said to me, “Son of man, these are the men who devise vain things and counsel wicked counsel in this city,
so that they may walk in My commands, keep My ordinances and carry them out. They will be My people, and I will be their God.
As their heart went toward the heart of their abominations and their lawlessness, I have brought their ways upon their heads, says the Lord.’”
The cherubim raised their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was upon them, above them.
The Lord’s glory rose from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain opposite the city.
A spirit lifted me and brought me into the Chaldeans’ land, to the captives, in a vision by God’s spirit. I rose out of the vision I had seen,
and I spoke to the captives all the Lord’s words that He had shown me.
who say, ‘Have the houses not been built recently? She is the cauldron, and we are the meat.’
Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man.”
The Lord’s spirit fell upon me, and He said to me, “Say, ‘Thus says the Lord: You have said this, house of Israel, and I understand the deliberations of your spirit.
You have multiplied your dead in this city and filled her roads with the wounded.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Your dead whom you struck within her are the meat, and she is the cauldron; but I will bring you out of her.
You fear the sword, and I will bring a sword upon you, says the Lord.
I will bring you out of her midst, hand you into foreigners’ hands, and execute judgments among you.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
Say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: The ruler and the leader in Jerusalem and in the whole house of Israel, who are among them—’
Say, ‘I perform portents in her midst. As I have done, so it will be for them; in deportation and captivity they will go.’

The ruler among them will be lifted upon shoulders and go out concealed through the wall. He will dig through it to go out through it. He will cover his face so that he may not be seen by an eye, and he himself will not see the land.
I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My enclosure. I will bring him to Babylon, to the Chaldeans’ land, and he will not see it, and there he will die.
All those around him, his helpers and all who support him, I will scatter to every wind; I will draw a sword after them.
They will know that I am the Lord when I scatter them among the nations, and I will disperse them among the countries.
I will spare a few men among them from sword, famine and death, so that they may recount all their lawlessness among the nations where they entered, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, eat your bread with pain, and drink your water with torment and distress,

and say to the people of the land, ‘Thus says the Lord to Jerusalem’s inhabitants upon Israel’s land: They will eat their bread with want and drink their water with devastation, so that the land may be destroyed with its fullness, for all who dwell in it are in impiety.
“Son of man, you dwell in the midst of their injustices. They have eyes to see and do not see, and ears to hear and do not hear, because they are an embittering house.
Their inhabited cities will be made desolate, and the land will be laid waste. You will recognize that I am the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, what is this proverb you have concerning Israel’s land, saying, ‘The days are far off; vision has perished’?

Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will turn back this proverb, and the house of Israel certainly will no longer say this proverb.’ For you will speak to them: ‘The days have drawn near, and the word of every vision,
because there will no longer be any false vision or anyone divining pleasing things among the sons of Israel,
because I, the Lord, will speak My words; I will speak and act, and I certainly will delay no longer. For in your days, embittering house, I will speak a word and act, says the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, behold, the embittering house of Israel keeps saying, ‘The vision this man sees is for many days ahead; this man prophesies of times far ahead.’
Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: None of My words that I may speak will be prolonged any longer. I will speak and act, says the Lord.’”

And you, son of man, get your belongings ready for captivity by day before them. You will be taken captive from your place to another place before them, so that they may see, because they are an embittering house.
You will bring your belongings out like belongings for captivity by day before their eyes, and you yourself will go out in the evening as a captive goes out.
Before them, dig for yourself through the wall, and you will pass out through it.
Before them you will be lifted upon shoulders and go out concealed. Cover your face, and you certainly will not see the land, for I have made you a portent to the house of Israel.”

I did so according to all that He commanded me. I brought belongings out like belongings for captivity by day; in the evening I dug through the wall for myself and went out concealed. I was lifted upon shoulders before them.
In the morning the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, has not the house of Israel, the embittering house, said to you, ‘What are you doing?’
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
Because they misled My people, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there was no peace, and this one builds a wall, and they coat it—if it is going to fall,

say to those coating it, ‘It will fall.’ There will be a flooding downpour, and I will put stones for hurling into their bonds, and they will fall; there will be an upending wind, and it will be split.
And behold, the wall has fallen! Will they not say to you, ‘Where is your coating with which you coated it?’
Therefore thus says the Lord: I will unleash an upending blast with wrath; a flooding downpour will come in My anger, and I will bring the projectile stones in wrath for complete destruction,

and I will tear down the wall you coated, and it will fall. I will lay it upon the ground; its foundations will be uncovered, and it will fall, and you will be brought to an end with rebukes. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
I will complete My wrath upon the wall and those coating it, and it will fall. I said to you, ‘There is no wall, nor those coating it—
the prophets of Israel who prophesy concerning Jerusalem and see peace for her, when there is no peace,’ says the Lord.’
And you, son of man, set your face firmly against the daughters of your people who prophesy from their own heart, and prophesy against them,

and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Woe to the women sewing cushions upon every elbow of an arm and making coverings upon every head of every age, to distort lives! The lives of My people were distorted, and they were preserving lives.

They were profaning Me among My people for a handful of barley and scraps of bread, putting to death lives that ought not die and preserving lives that ought not live, as you uttered things to a people listening to vain pronouncements.
“Son of man, prophesy against Israel’s prophets; you will prophesy and say to them, ‘Hear the Lord’s word!

Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against your cushions, on which you entangle lives. I will tear them from your arms and send the lives out—their lives that you twist away—into dispersion.
I will tear your coverings and rescue My people from your hand. They will no longer be in your hands for entanglement, and you will recognize that I am the Lord.
Because you distorted the righteous person’s heart unjustly, though I was not distorting him, and strengthened the lawless person’s hands so that he does not turn at all from his evil way and live,
therefore you certainly will no longer see false things or divine divinations. I will rescue My people from your hand, and you will know that I am the Lord.’”
Thus says the Lord: Woe to those who prophesy from their own heart and see nothing at all!
Your prophets, Israel, are like foxes in the wildernesses.
They did not stand in a firm position, and they gathered flocks against the house of Israel. Those saying, ‘On the Lord’s day,’ did not rise.
They see false things and divine vain things, those who say, ‘The Lord says,’ although the Lord has not sent them; and they began to establish a word.
Have you not seen a false vision and spoken vain divinations?
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because your words are false and your divinations vain, therefore behold, I am against you, says the Lord,

and I will stretch out My hand against the prophets who see false things and utter vain things. They will not belong to My people’s instruction, nor be written in the register of the house of Israel, nor enter Israel’s land. They will know that I am the Lord.
Men from Israel’s elders came to me and sat before me.
They will receive their injustice; according to the inquirer’s offense and according to the offense, it will likewise be for the prophet,
so that the house of Israel may no longer wander from Me or be defiled by any of their transgressions. They will be My people, and I will be their God, says the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, if a land sins against Me by committing a transgression, and I stretch My hand against it, shatter its support of bread, send famine upon it, and remove human and livestock from it,
even if these three men—Noah, Daniel and Job—were within it, they themselves would be saved by their righteousness, says the Lord.
Even if I bring evil beasts upon the land and punish it, so that it becomes a devastation and no one passes through because of the beasts,
and these three men were within it, as I live, says the Lord, neither sons nor daughters would be saved; only they themselves would be saved, and the land would be destroyed.
Or even if I bring a sword upon that land and say, ‘Let a sword pass through the land,’ and remove human and livestock from it,
and these three men were within it, as I live, says the Lord, they certainly would not rescue sons or daughters; they alone would be saved.
Or even if I send death upon that land and pour My wrath upon it in blood, to destroy human and livestock from it,
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
and Noah, Daniel and Job were within it, as I live, says the Lord, neither sons nor daughters would be left; they would rescue their own lives by their righteousness.
Thus says the Lord: Even if I send My four evil retributions—sword, famine, evil beasts and death—against Jerusalem, to destroy human and livestock from her,

and behold, her rescued survivors are left in her, bringing sons and daughters out of her. Behold, they are coming out to you. You will see their ways and their reflections and feel regret over the evils I brought upon Jerusalem—all the evils I brought upon her,
and they will comfort you, because you will see their ways and their reflections, and recognize that I have not done in vain all that I did in her, says the Lord.”
“Son of man, these men have set their thoughts upon their hearts and set the punishment of their injustices before their faces. Shall I indeed answer them?

Therefore speak to them and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: Anyone of the house of Israel who sets his thoughts upon his heart, places the punishment of his injustice before his face, and comes to the prophet—I, the Lord, will answer him in the things in which his mind is entangled,
so that it may turn the house of Israel aside in accordance with their hearts, alienated from Me through their reflections.’
Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Turn back and turn away from your practices and all your impieties, and turn your faces.

For anyone of the house of Israel or of the sojourners living among Israel who becomes alienated from Me, sets his reflections upon his heart, places the punishment of his injustice before his face, and comes to the prophet to question him concerning Me—I, the Lord, will answer him in that in which he is entangled.
I will set My face firmly against that person, make him a wilderness and a devastation, and remove him from the midst of My people. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
If the prophet is led astray and speaks, I, the Lord, have led that prophet astray. I will stretch out My hand against him and destroy him from the midst of My people Israel.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“And you, son of man, what could vinewood be among all the branch wood found among the forest trees?
Will they take wood from it to make anything useful? Will they take a peg from it to hang any vessel upon it?
It has only been given to the fire to be consumed. Fire consumes its yearly prunings, and it is utterly spent. Surely it will not be useful for work?
Even when it is whole, it will not serve for work. How much less if fire consumes it completely—will it still serve for work?
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: As with the vinewood among the forest trees, which I have given to the fire to be consumed, so I have given Jerusalem’s inhabitants.
I will set My face against them. They will come out of the fire, and fire will devour them. They will recognize that I am the Lord when I set My face firmly against them.
I will lay the land waste, because they have fallen into transgression, says the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
and clothed you in patterned garments, gave you blue-purple footwear, girded you with fine linen, and wrapped you in hair-woven cloth,
and adorned you with ornaments, placed bracelets around your hands and a necklace around your neck,
and put a ring around your nostril, little hoops upon your ears and a crown of boasting upon your head.
You were adorned with gold and silver; your coverings were fine linen, hair-woven and patterned. You ate fine flour, oil and honey, and became very beautiful.
Your fame went out among the nations because of your beauty, for it was made complete in splendor, in the loveliness I placed upon you, says the Lord.
You trusted in your beauty and prostituted yourself because of your fame. You poured out your prostitution upon every passerby—which will not be.
You took some of your garments, made sewn idols for yourself and prostituted yourself upon them. You certainly will not enter, nor will it come to be.
You took your vessels of boasting from My gold and My silver, from what I had given you, made male images for yourself and prostituted yourself among them.
You took your patterned clothing and clothed them; you set My oil and My incense before them.
My loaves that I gave you—fine flour, oil and honey with which I fed you—you set before them as a fragrant aroma. So it happened, says the Lord.
“Son of man, solemnly testify to Jerusalem about her lawlessness,
You took your sons and daughters whom you had borne and sacrificed them to them for consumption, as though you had prostituted yourself only a little,
and slaughtered your children and gave them over as you used them for averting rites.
This was in addition to all your prostitution, and you did not remember the days of your infancy, when you were naked and exposed and lived befouled in your blood.
After all your evils, says the Lord,
you built yourself a prostitution chamber and made yourself a display place in every broad street,
and at the head of every road you built your brothels, ruined your beauty, spread your legs to every passerby, and multiplied your prostitution.
You prostituted yourself with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors great in flesh, and prostituted yourself in many ways to anger Me.

But if I stretch My hand against you, I will remove your ordinances and hand you over to the desires of those who hate you, daughters of foreigners who turn you aside from your way in which you acted impiously.
You prostituted yourself with the daughters of Assyria, and not even so were you filled; you prostituted yourself, and were not filled.
You multiplied your covenants toward the Chaldeans’ land, and not even with these were you filled.
and say, ‘Thus says the Lord to Jerusalem: Your root and your birth are from the land of Canaan; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.
What shall I do to your daughter, says the Lord, when you do all these things, the works of a prostitute? And you prostituted yourself threefold
among your daughters. You built your brothel at every road head and made your platform in every broad street, and became like a prostitute gathering payments.
The adulterous wife is like you, receiving payments from her husband;
she kept giving payments to all who prostituted her. You too gave payments to all your lovers and loaded them up to come to you from all around in your prostitution.

With you it became distorted compared with other women in your prostitution. They have prostituted themselves with you as you paid extra payments, and no payments were given to you; with you things became distorted.
Therefore, prostitute, hear the Lord’s word!

Thus says the Lord: Because you poured out your copper, your shame will be exposed in your prostitution with your lovers, in all the reflections of your lawlessness, and in the blood of your children whom you gave to them.

Therefore behold, I am gathering against you all your lovers with whom you mingled, all whom you loved together with all whom you hated. I will gather them against you from all around, reveal your evils to them, and they will see all your shame.
I will exact retribution upon you with the retribution of an adulteress and a woman shedding blood, and place you in blood of wrath and jealousy.
I will hand you into their hands. They will tear down your brothel, pull down your platform, strip your clothing from you, take your vessels of boasting, and leave you naked and exposed.
As for your birth, on the day you were born they did not bind your breasts; you were not washed with water, not salted with salt, and not wrapped in swaddling cloths.
They will bring crowds against you, stone you with stones, and slaughter you with their swords.
They will burn your houses with fire and exact retributions upon you before many women. I will turn you away from your prostitution, and you certainly will give no more payments.
I will release My wrath upon you; My jealousy will be removed from you. I will rest and certainly be concerned no longer.

Because you did not remember the day of your infancy but grieved Me with all these things, behold, I have brought your ways upon your head, says the Lord. Thus you committed impiety in addition to all your lawlessness.
These are all the things they said against you in a proverb, saying, ‘As the mother, so the daughter.’

You are the daughter of your mother, who rejected her husband and her children, and the sister of your sisters, who rejected their husbands and children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
Your elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters, dwelling at your left; your sister younger than you, dwelling at your right, is Sodom and her daughters.
Not even so did you walk in their ways or act according to their lawlessness. Before long, you surpass them in all your ways.
As I live, says the Lord, your sister Sodom, she and her daughters, certainly did not do as you and your daughters have done.

Yet this was the lawlessness of your sister Sodom: arrogance. In fullness of bread and abundance of wine she and her daughters lived luxuriously. This belonged to her and her daughters, but they did not support the hand of the poor and needy.
Nor did My eye spare you to do any of all these things for you, to feel anything for you. You were cast upon the face of the plain because of your life’s crookedness, on the day you were born.
They boasted greatly and committed acts of lawlessness before Me, and I removed them as I saw.
Samaria did not sin half your sins. You multiplied your lawlessness beyond theirs and justified your sisters by all the lawlessness you committed.

You too, receive your torment, in which you corrupted your sisters by your sins, in which you acted more lawlessly than they and justified them above yourself. You too, be ashamed and take your dishonor, in that you justified your sisters.
I will reverse their reversals—the reversal of Sodom and her daughters; I will reverse the reversal of Samaria and her daughters; and I will reverse your reversal among them,
so that you may receive your torment and be dishonored for all you did in provoking Me.

Your sister Sodom and her daughters will be restored as they were from the beginning; Samaria and her daughters will be restored as they were from the beginning; and you and your daughters will be restored as you were from the beginning.
And if your sister Sodom was not a report in your mouth in the days of your arrogance,
before your evils were revealed—as now you are a reproach of Syria’s daughters and all around her, daughters of foreigners who surround you all around?
Your impieties and your lawlessness—you have borne them, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: I will deal with you as you have done, as you dishonored these things by transgressing My covenant.
I passed by you and saw you befouled in your blood, and said to you, ‘From your blood, life!
I Myself will remember My covenant with you in the days of your infancy and raise up for you an eternal covenant.

You will remember your way and be dishonored when you take up your sisters, those older than you together with those younger than you. I will give them to you for building up, and not from your covenant.
I Myself will raise up My covenant with you, and you will recognize that I am the Lord,
so that you may remember and be ashamed, and no longer have occasion to open your mouth because of your dishonor, when I am propitious to you concerning all that you have done, says the Lord.’”
Multiply!’ I have made you like the growth of the field. You multiplied, grew great and entered cities of cities. Your breasts stood firm and your hair grew, but you were naked and exposed.

I passed through you and saw you; behold, your season was the season of those lodging. I spread My wings over you and covered your exposure. I swore to you and entered a covenant with you, says the Lord, and you became Mine.
I washed you with water, washed your blood off you, and anointed you with oil,
You will say, ‘Why did the son not receive his father’s injustice?’ Because the son practiced righteousness and mercy, preserved all My ordinances and carried them out; he will surely live.

The soul that sins will die. The son will not receive his father’s injustice, nor the father his son’s injustice. The righteous person’s righteousness will be upon him, and the lawless person’s lawlessness upon him.
If the lawless person turns from all the lawlessness he committed, keeps all My commandments, and practices righteousness and mercy, he will surely live; he certainly will not die.
The house of Israel says, ‘The Lord’s way does not go right.’ Surely My way does not fail to go right, house of Israel? Is it not your way that fails to go right?
I will judge you, each according to his way, house of Israel, says the Lord. Turn back and turn away from all your impieties, and they will not become a punishment of injustice for you.
Cast away from yourselves all your impieties with which you acted impiously against Me, and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why are you dying, house of Israel?
For I do not desire the death of the one who dies, says the Lord.”
“And you, take up a lament over Israel’s ruler,
and fire went out from a rod of her choice parts and devoured her, and there was no rod of strength in her. A tribe is for a parable of lament, and it will become a lament.”
And it happened in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth of the month, while I was among the captives by the River Chebar: the heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.
The likeness of their faces was a human face and a lion’s face on the right for all four, and a calf’s face on the left for all four, and an eagle’s face for all four.
The wings of all four were stretched out above; each had two joined to one another, and two covered the top of their bodies.
Each went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit was going, they went and did not turn.
And amid the living creatures was an appearance like burning coals of fire, like the sight of torches whirling among the living creatures, and brightness of the fire; lightning came out of the fire.
I looked, and behold, one wheel was on the earth adjoining the four living creatures;
the appearance of the wheels was like the appearance of tharsis, and all four had one likeness; their workmanship was as though a wheel were within a wheel.
They went toward their four sides; they did not turn as they went,
nor did their backs; they were tall, and I saw them. The backs of all four were full of eyes all around.
When the living creatures went, the wheels moved beside them; when the living creatures rose from the earth, the wheels rose.
On the fifth of the month—this was the fifth year of King Jehoiakim’s captivity—
Wherever the cloud was, there was the spirit for movement; the living creatures and the wheels went and rose together with them, because a spirit of life was in the wheels.
When they went, these went; when they stood, these stood; when they rose from the earth, these rose together with them, because a spirit of life was in the wheels.
Above the living creatures’ heads was a likeness as of a firmament, like the appearance of crystal, stretched out above their wings;
and beneath the firmament their wings were stretched out, fluttering one toward another; each had two joined together, covering their bodies.
As they went, I heard the sound of their wings like the sound of much water; when they stood, their wings came to rest.
And behold, a voice came from above the firmament that was over their heads.
Like the appearance of a sapphire stone was the likeness of a throne upon it; and above the likeness of the throne was a likeness like the form of a human being.

I saw something like the sight of electrum from the appearance of a waist upward; and from the appearance of a waist down below I saw something like the appearance of fire, with its brightness all around.
the Lord’s word came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the River Chebar; and the Lord’s hand came upon me,

and I looked, and behold, a sweeping wind was coming from the north, and a great cloud was within it, with brightness around it and fire flashing like lightning; within it was something like the appearance of electrum, within the fire, and brightness within it.
And within it was something like a likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: a human likeness was upon them,
and each had four faces, and each had four wings.
Their legs were straight, and their feet were winged, with sparks like flashing bronze; and their wings were light.
A human hand was beneath their wings on their four sides; and the faces of all four of them
did not turn as they walked; each went straight ahead.
In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, men from the elders of the house of Israel came to question the Lord and sat before me.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“And you, son of man, will you judge the city of bloodshed? Display all her lawless deeds to her,
and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: O city shedding blood within her so that her time may come, making reflections against herself to defile herself!

Through their blood that you shed you have transgressed, and through your reflections that you made you were being defiled. You brought your days near and brought the season of your years. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all the countries
near you and far away from you. They will mock you: “Unclean, the famous one, abundant in lawless deeds!”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
I saw that she was defiled; one way for the two.
She added to her prostitution and saw men depicted upon the wall, images of Chaldeans drawn with a stylus,
girded with embroidered work at their waists, with dyed tiaras upon their heads, all with a threefold appearance, the likeness of Chaldeans’ sons from their native land.
She set her desire upon them at the sight of her eyes and sent messengers to them in the Chaldeans’ land.
Babylon’s sons came to her, to a bed of lodgers, and defiled her in her prostitution. She was defiled by them, and her soul withdrew from them.
She uncovered her prostitution and uncovered her shame. My soul withdrew from her, as My soul had withdrawn from her sister.
“Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother,

I will set My jealousy within you, and they will deal with you in fierce anger. They will remove your nose and ears and strike down your remaining people with the sword. They will take your sons and daughters, and fire will consume your remaining people.
They will strip you of your clothing and take the objects of your boasting.
I will turn your impieties away from you and your prostitution from Egypt’s land. You certainly will not lift your eyes toward them, and you certainly will no longer remember Egypt.
For thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am handing you into the hands of those you hate, those from whom your soul withdrew.

They will deal with you in hatred and take all the fruit of your pain and toil. You will be naked and exposed to shame, and the shame of your prostitution and your impiety will be uncovered. Your prostitution
and they prostituted themselves in Egypt in their youth. There their breasts fell; there they were deflowered.
did these things to you when you prostituted yourself after nations and were defiled in their reflections.
Their names were Oholah the elder and Oholibah her sister. They became Mine and bore sons and daughters. Their names: Samaria is Oholah, and Jerusalem is Oholibah.
Righteous men will punish them with the punishment of an adulteress and the punishment of bloodshed, for they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands.
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Bring a multitude against them and set turmoil and plunder among them,
and stone them with the multitude’s stones and pierce them with their swords. They will kill their sons and daughters and burn their houses.
I will turn impiety away from the land. All women will be disciplined and certainly will not act according to their impieties.
Your impiety will be brought upon you, and you will receive the sins of your reflections. You will know that I am the Lord.”
Oholah prostituted herself away from Me and set her desire upon her lovers, the Assyrians approaching her,
clothed in blue-purple, leaders and generals; all choice young men, horsemen riding horses.
She bestowed her prostitution upon them, all choice sons of Assyrians; and with all upon whom she set her desire, in all her reflections she was defiled.
She did not abandon her prostitution from Egypt, for they lay with her in her youth; they deflowered her and poured their prostitution upon her.
The Lord’s word came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, saying,
I spoke to the people in the morning as He commanded me, and my wife died in the evening. In the morning I did as I was ordered.
The people said to me, “Will you not tell us what these things are that you are doing?”
“Son of man, write for yourself a record of the day, from this day on which Babylon’s king pressed against Jerusalem, from this present day,
I said to them, “The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
with your hair upon your heads and your footwear on your feet. You certainly will neither beat your breasts nor weep; you will waste away in your injustices and each will comfort his brother.
Ezekiel will be a portent for you; according to everything he has done, you will do when these things come. You will recognize that I am the Lord.

And you, son of man, will it not be on the day when I take their strength from them, the exaltation of their boasting, the desires of their eyes, the exaltation of their soul, their sons and daughters—
and speak a parable against the provoking house. Say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: Set on the cauldron and pour water into it,
and put the cut pieces into it, every good cut, leg and shoulder stripped from the bones,
from choice animals taken. Burn the bones beneath them. It boiled, it boiled, and her bones have been cooked within her.
Therefore thus says the Lord: O city of bloodshed! A cauldron with rust in it, whose rust has not come out of her! He brought it out limb by limb; no lot fell upon her.
For her blood is within her. I have set it upon smooth rock; I have not poured it upon the earth to cover it with earth.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, take up a lament over the ruler of Tyre and say to him: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: You were a seal of likeness and a crown of beauty;

you came to be in the delight of God’s paradise. You have been clothed with every good stone: carnelian, topaz, emerald, carbuncle, sapphire, jasper, silver, gold, ligurite, agate, amethyst, chrysolite, beryl, and onyx. You filled your treasuries and storehouses within you with gold from the day you were created.
With the cherub I placed you on God’s holy mountain; you came to be among fiery stones.
You were blameless in your days from the day you were created until wrongdoings were found in you.
From the abundance of your trade you filled your store chambers with lawlessness, and you sinned and were wounded away from God’s mountain; the cherub led you out from among fiery stones.

Your heart was exalted because of your beauty; your knowledge was corrupted together with your beauty. Because of your many sins I threw you to the ground; I placed you before kings to be made a spectacle.

Because of your many sins and the wrongdoings of your trade you profaned your sacred places. I will bring fire out from within you; it will consume you. I will turn you to ashes on your land before all who see you.

And you, son of man, do not fear them or be shaken before their faces, because they will rage and gather against you all around, and you dwell among scorpions. Do not fear their words or be shaken before their faces, for it is an embittering house.
You will speak My words to them, if indeed they listen or are terrified, for it is an embittering house.
And you, son of man, hear the One speaking to you. Do not become embittering like the embittering house. Open your mouth wide and eat what I give you.”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, those dwelling in the devastated places upon Israel’s land say, ‘Abraham was one, yet he possessed the land. We are more; the land has been given to us as a possession.’
Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord:
I will sanctify My great name, profaned among the nations, which you profaned among them. The nations will know that I am the Lord when I am sanctified in you before their eyes.
I will take you out of the nations, gather you out of all the lands and bring you into your own land.
I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you will be cleansed from all your uncleannesses and all your idols. I will cleanse you.
And I will give you a new heart, and I will give a new spirit within you; and I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh, and give you a heart of flesh.
I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments and do them.
You will dwell upon the land I gave your fathers. You will be My people, and I will be your God.
I will save you from all your uncleannesses, summon the grain and multiply it, and will not bring famine upon you.
I will multiply the tree’s fruit and the field’s produce, so that you do not bear the reproach of famine among the nations.
You will remember your evil ways and practices that were not good, and feel disgust before them at your lawless deeds and abominations.
I am not acting because of you, says the Lord, the Lord; this will be known to you. Be ashamed and abashed because of your ways, house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord: On the day I cleanse you from all your lawless deeds, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the wilderness places will be rebuilt.
I will make them one nation in My land and upon Israel’s mountains, and one ruler will be theirs. They will no longer be two nations or ever again be divided into two kingdoms,

so that they no longer defile themselves with their idols. I will deliver them from all their lawless deeds in which they sinned and cleanse them. They will be My people, and I, the Lord, will be their God.
My servant David will be ruler among them, and one shepherd will be over all, because they will walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments and do them.
They will dwell upon their land, which I gave My servant Jacob, where their fathers dwelt. They will dwell upon it, and David My servant will be their ruler for ever.
I will make a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant with them. I will set My holy things among them for ever.
My dwelling will be among them. I will be their God, and they will be My people.

The four sides were measured with the same reed. He laid it out, with their enclosure all around: five hundred toward the east and five hundred cubits in breadth, to distinguish between the holy areas and the forewall in the arrangement of the house.
He led me to the gate facing east and brought me out.

Look—the glory of the God of Israel was coming by the way of the gate facing east. The sound of the camp was like the sound of many redoubling their sound, and the earth flashed like radiance from the glory all around.
The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when I was entering to anoint the city; and the vision of the chariot I saw was like the vision I had seen by the River Chobar. I fall on my face.
The glory of the Lord entered the house by the way of the gate facing east.
A spirit lifted me and brought me into the inner court. Look—the house was full of the glory of the Lord.
I stood, and look—a voice from the house, speaking to me, while the man stood next to me.
He said to me, “Behold, I have given you cattle dung instead of human dung; prepare your loaves over it.”
He said to me, “Son of man, behold, I am breaking the support of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight and in need, and drink water by measure and in devastation,
so that they become needy for bread and water. A man and his brother will disappear, and they will waste away in their injustices.

A quarter of you will be consumed by death; a quarter of you will perish by famine within you; a quarter of you I will scatter to every wind; and a quarter of you will fall by the sword around you, and I will draw a sword after them.
My wrath and My anger against them will be completed, and you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken in My jealousy when I complete My anger against them.
I will make you a wilderness, and your daughters around you, before every passerby;
They will recognize that I, the Lord, have spoken.
Thus says the Lord: Clap your hand, stamp your foot, and say, “Aha! Aha!” over all the abominations of the house of Israel; they will fall by sword, death and famine.
wounded people will fall in your midst, and you will recognize that I am the Lord.
When there are among you survivors of the sword among the nations, and in your scattering in the lands,

the survivors from among you will remember Me among the nations where they were taken captive. I have sworn against their heart that whores away from Me and their eyes that whore after their pursuits; they will beat their faces over all their abominations.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
Behold, the end has come; behold, the Lord’s day! Even if the rod has blossomed, insolence has risen.
“And you, son of man, say, ‘Thus says the Lord to the land of Israel: An end has come; the end has come upon the four wings of the land.
The end has come
upon you, inhabitant of the land. The time has come; the day has drawn near, neither with tumult nor with birth pangs.
Now soon I will pour My anger upon you and complete My wrath in you; I will judge you in your ways and bring all your abominations upon you.
Now the end is upon you. I Myself will send against you and exact retribution upon you in your ways; I will bring all your abominations upon you.
My eye will not spare you, nor will I have mercy; I will bring your way upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
For thus says the Lord:
and there were seventy men from the elders of the house of Israel. Jaazaniah son of Shaphan stood among them before their faces; each had his censer in his hand, and the vapor of incense rose.
He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel do, each in their hidden bedchamber? For they said, ‘The Lord does not see; the Lord has abandoned the land.’”
He said to me, “You will yet see greater lawlessness that these people are committing.”
and I saw, and behold, the likeness of a man: from His waist downward, fire, and from His waist upward, like the appearance of electrum.

He stretched out the likeness of a hand and lifted me by the crown of my head. A spirit lifted me between earth and heaven and brought me to Jerusalem in a vision of God, to the entrance of the inner gate facing north, where the pillar of the one acquiring stood.
And behold, the glory of the Lord God of Israel was there, in accordance with the vision I had seen in the plain.
He cried into my ears with a loud voice, saying, “The city’s retribution has drawn near.” Each had the implements of destruction in his hand.
My eye will not spare, nor will I have mercy. I have brought their ways upon their heads.”
And behold, the man wearing the full-length robe, with the belt fastened at his waist, answered, saying, “I have done as Thou didst command me.”

And behold, six men came from the direction of the high gate facing north, each with an axe in his hand. One man among them wore a full-length robe, with a sapphire belt at his waist. They entered and stood beside the bronze altar.
The glory of the God of Israel, which had been upon the cherubim, rose from them to the forecourt of the house. He called the man wearing the full-length robe, who had the belt at his waist,
and said to him, “Pass through the midst of Jerusalem and put the sign upon the foreheads of the men who sigh deeply and grieve over all the lawlessness being committed within her.”
To these others He said while I listened, “Go behind him into the city and strike. Do not spare with your eyes, and have no mercy.

Old man, young man, maiden, infants and women—kill them to obliteration. But do not approach anyone upon whom the sign is. Begin at My holy places.” They began with the elderly men who were inside the house.
He said to them, “Defile the house and fill the roads with the dead as you go out, and strike.”
As they struck, I fall upon my face and cried aloud and said, “Alas, Lord! Art Thou obliterating the survivors of Israel as Thou pourest out Thy wrath upon Jerusalem?”

He said to me, “The injustice of the house of Israel and Judah has grown very, very great, because the land is full of many peoples, and the city full of injustice and uncleanness. For they said, ‘The Lord has abandoned the land; the Lord does not look upon it.’
The sun rose upon the earth, and Lot entered into Zoar.
And the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah sulphur and fire from the Lord out of the heaven;
and He overthrew those cities, and all the surrounding country, and all that lived in the cities, and all that sprang from the earth.
And his wife looked behind her, and became a pillar of salt.
Now Abraham was old, advanced in days; and the Lord had blessed Abraham in all things.
And before he had finished speaking in his mind, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, having her water jar upon her shoulder.
Now the maiden was very beautiful to look at; she was a virgin, and no man had known her. And she went down to the spring, and filled her water jar, and came up.
And the servant ran to meet her, and said, “Give me a little water to drink from your water jar.”
And she said, “Drink, my lord.” And she hurried, and lowered her water jar upon her arm, and gave him to drink,
until he ceased drinking. And she said, “I will draw water for your camels also, until they have all drunk.”
And Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his house, who ruled over all that he had, “Put your hand under my thigh,
And she hurried, and emptied her water jar into the trough, and ran again to the well to draw water; and she drew water for all the camels.
And the man watched her, and remained silent, to know whether the Lord had prospered his journey or not.
And when all the camels had ceased drinking, the man took golden earrings, each a drachma in weight, and two bracelets for her hands, ten gold pieces in weight.
And he asked her, and said, “Whose daughter are you? Tell me, is there room with your father for us to lodge?”
and I will make you swear by the Lord, the God of the heaven and the God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son Isaac from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell;
but you shall go to my land, where I was born, and to my tribe, and take a wife for my son Isaac from there.”
And she hurried, and lowered her water jar, and said, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels.’ And I drank, and she watered my camels.

And I asked her, and said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ And she said, ‘I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.’ And I put the earrings upon her, and the bracelets about her hands.

And I was well pleased, and worshipped the Lord, and blessed the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who had prospered my way in the way of truth, to take the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.
And the servant said to him, “Perhaps the woman will not be willing to follow me to this land; shall I bring your son back to the land from where you came?”
And Abraham said to him, “Take care not to bring my son back there.

The Lord, the God of the heaven and the God of the earth, who took me from my father’s house and from the land where I was born, who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, ‘I will give this land to you, and to your seed,’ He shall send His angel before you; and you shall take a wife for my son Isaac from there.
And Noah begot three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And Noah did all that the Lord God commanded him; so he did.
But Noah found grace before the Lord God.
These are the generations of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah pleased God.
And the Lord God said to Noah, “Enter the ark, you and all your household, for I have seen you righteous before Me in this generation.
“Of the clean animals, bring in with you by sevens, male and female; and of the unclean animals, by twos, male and female.
“And surely I will require your blood, the blood of your lives. From every beast I will require it, and from the hand of a fellow man I will require the life of man.
Whoever sheds the blood of man, his own blood shall be shed in return; for in the image of God I made man.
“But you, grow and multiply, and fill the earth and multiply upon it.”
The Lord answered me: “Write a vision clearly on a boxwood tablet, so that the one reading these things may pursue them.
For the vision is still for a season, and it will rise toward the end and not toward emptiness. If he delays, wait for him, for coming he will come and certainly will not linger.
If he draws back, My soul has no pleasure in him; but the righteous one shall live by My faithfulness.

The number of Israel’s sons was like the sand of the sea, which will not be measured or counted. In the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ there they will be called sons of the living God.
She did not know that it was I who gave her grain, wine and oil and multiplied silver for her; but she made silver and gold objects for Baal.
Therefore I will return and recover My grain at its season and My wine at its time; I will take away My garments and linen cloths so that they do not cover her shame.
Now I will uncover her uncleanness before her lovers, and certainly no one will deliver her from My hand.
I will turn away all her rejoicings, her festivals, new moons and Sabbaths, and all her festal assemblies.

I will obliterate her vine and fig trees, of which she said, ‘These are my wages that my lovers gave me.’ I will make them a testimony, and the field’s beasts, heaven’s birds and the earth’s creeping things will devour them.”
“I will exact vengeance upon her for the days of the Baalim, when she sacrificed to them, put on her earrings and necklaces and went after her lovers, but forgot Me,” says the Lord.
“Therefore look, I am leading her astray; I will place her in a wilderness and speak to her heart,
and from there I will give her her possessions and the Valley of Achor to open her understanding. There she will be humbled as in the days of her infancy and the days of her ascent from Egypt’s land.
On that day,” says the Lord, “she will call Me ‘My Husband’ and no longer call Me ‘Baalim.’
I will remove the names of the Baalim from her mouth, and they will certainly no longer remember their names.
Judah’s sons and Israel’s sons will gather together, appoint one authority for themselves and come up from the land, for great is Jezreel’s day.
On that day I will establish a covenant for them with the field’s beasts, heaven’s birds and the earth’s creeping things. I will shatter bow, sword and war from the land and settle you in hope.
I will betroth you to Myself forever; I will betroth you to Myself in righteousness and judgment, in mercy and compassion,
and I will betroth you to Myself in faithfulness, and you will know the Lord.
On that day,” says the Lord, “I will listen to heaven, and heaven will listen to the earth,
and the earth will listen to grain, wine and oil, and they will listen to Jezreel.
I will sow her for Myself upon the land, show mercy to Not Shown Mercy and say to Not My People, ‘You are My people.’ He will say, ‘Thou art the Lord my God!’”
Say to your brother, ‘My People,’ and to your sister, ‘Shown Mercy.’
“Enter into judgment with your mother, enter into judgment! For she is not My wife and I am not her husband. I will remove her prostitution from My face and her adultery from between her breasts,
so that I may strip her naked and restore her as on the day of her birth. I will make her like a wilderness, set her like a waterless land and kill her with thirst.
I will certainly show no mercy to her children, for they are children of prostitution.

For their mother prostituted herself; she who bore them brought shame. She said, ‘I will follow my lovers, who give me my loaves and water, my garments and linen cloths, my oil and everything due to me.’
Therefore look, I block her way with thorns and will build up her roads, and she will certainly not find her path.

She will pursue her lovers but certainly not catch them; she will seek them but certainly not find them. She will say, ‘I will go and return to my former husband, for it was better for me then than now.’
The Lord said to me, “Go again and love a woman who loves evil things and is an adulteress, just as God loves Israel’s sons, though they look toward foreign gods and love cakes with raisins.”
I hired her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver, a gomor of barley and a nebel of wine.
Therefore they will be handed over among the nations. Now I will receive them, and they will pause a little from anointing a king and rulers.
Israel was swallowed up; now he became among the nations like a useless vessel.
Because they went up to the Assyrians; Ephraim flourished by himself, and they loved gifts.
I will give him David’s glory, and he will rule, with no one contradicting.
I will establish him as a ruler in a trustworthy place, and he will become a throne of glory for his father’s house.
Every glorious person in his father’s house, from small to great, will trust in him, and they will hang upon him.
On that day—thus says the Lord Sabaoth—the person established in a trustworthy place will be shaken and fall, and the glory upon him will be removed, because the Lord has spoken.”
The vision of Tyre. Wail, ships of Carthage, because she has perished, and they no longer come from the Kitians’ land; she has been led captive.
therefore thus says the Lord: “Behold, I will place in Zion’s foundations a costly, chosen, precious cornerstone, in her foundations, and whoever trusts in it will certainly not be ashamed.
I will make judgment a hope, and My mercy will be weights; those trusting deceit do so in vain, for a storm will certainly not pass you by—
might it also remove your covenant with death? Your hope toward Hades will certainly not remain. If a rushing storm comes, you will become its trampling ground.
It will be shade from heat, shelter and concealment from harshness and rain.
For as rain or snow comes down from the heaven, and does not return until it has drenched the earth, and made it bring forth and sprout, and given seed to the sower and bread for food,
so it will be with My word, whatever goes out from My mouth: it will certainly not return until all that I have willed is accomplished; and I will prosper your ways and My commandments.
For you will go out in gladness, and in joy you will be taught; for the mountains and the hills will leap, welcoming you with joy, and all the trees of the field will clap their branches.
But as the heaven is distant from the earth, so is My way distant from your ways, and your thoughts from My mind.
I will sing now to the beloved a song of the loved one for my vineyard. The beloved had a vineyard on a horn, in a fertile place.
I put a fence around it, surrounded it with a palisade, planted a Sorech vine, built a tower in its midst and dug a wine vat in it. I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
Now, man of Judah and residents of Jerusalem, judge My case and the matter of My vineyard.
What more shall I do for My vineyard that I did not do for it? For I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
Now I will announce to you what I will do to My vineyard: I will remove its fence, and it will be plundered; I will pull down its wall, and it will be trampled,
and I will abandon My vineyard. It will certainly not be pruned or dug, and thorns will rise in it as in fallow ground. I will command the clouds not to rain upon it.
For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is Israel’s house, and the man of Judah a beloved new planting. I waited for it to produce judgment, but it produced lawlessness, not righteousness but an outcry.
Woe to those joining house to house and bringing field beside field, so that they may take something from their neighbor! Surely you will not dwell alone upon the earth?
Shine, shine, Jerusalem, for your light has come, and the Lord’s glory has risen upon you.
Behold, darkness and gloom will cover earth over nations, but the Lord will appear upon you, and His glory will be seen over you.
Kings will walk by your light, and nations by your radiance.
Lift your eyes around you and see your children gathered. Behold, all your sons have come from far away, and your daughters will be lifted upon shoulders.
This is what you will say to them: Gods who did not make heaven and earth, let them perish from the earth and from beneath this heaven.
They must be lifted and carried, because they will not take a step. Do not fear them, because they certainly will not do evil, and no good is in them.
It is worked silver; they will not walk. Applied silver will come from Tarshish, gold from Mophaz, and the goldsmiths’ hand; all are artisans’ works. They will dress them in blue and purple.
And I said: O Lord, behold, their prophets prophesy and say, ‘You will not see sword, nor will famine be among you, because I will give truth and peace upon the land and in this place.’

And the Lord said to me: The prophets prophesy false things in My name; I did not send them or command them or speak to them, because they prophesy false visions, divinations, omens, and their heart’s choices to you.

Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the prophets prophesying false things in My name, though I did not send them, who say, ‘Sword and famine will not be upon this land’: They will die a diseased death, and the prophets will be consumed by famine.

And the people to whom they prophesy will be thrown into Jerusalem’s thoroughfares because of sword and famine, and there will be no one burying them, and their wives and sons and daughters; and I will pour their evils upon them.
And you will say this word to them: Bring tears down upon your eyes day and night, and let them not cease, because the daughter of My people was utterly crushed, with a very painful wound.
Because of these things the land mourned and the wilderness pastures dried up. Their course became evil, and their strength was not so.
Because priest and prophet were defiled, and in My house I saw their evils.
Therefore let their way become a slippery place for them in darkness, and they will be tripped and fall in it, because I will bring evils upon them in their year of visitation, says the Lord.
And among Samaria’s prophets I saw lawless acts: they prophesied through Baal and led My people Israel astray.

And among Jerusalem’s prophets I have seen horrifying things: committing adultery, walking in lies, and supporting evil hands so that no one turns from his evil way. They all became like Sodom to Me, and her inhabitants like Gomorrah.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will feed them pain and give them bitter water to drink, because from Jerusalem’s prophets defilement went out into all the land.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Do not listen to the prophets’ words, because they make a vision futile for themselves. They speak from their own heart and not from the Lord’s mouth.

They say to those rejecting the Lord’s word, You will have peace. To all who walk according to their own wishes, to everyone walking in the wandering of his heart, they said, No evils will come upon you.
And the Lord’s fury will no longer turn back until He does it and raises it up from His heart’s undertaking. At the end of the days they will understand these things.
I was not sending the prophets, yet they ran; I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.
And if they had stood in My standing presence and listened to My words, they would have turned My people from their evil practices.
Are not My words like blazing fire, says the Lord, and like an axe cutting rock?
Therefore behold, I am against the prophets, says the Lord God, who steal My words, each from his neighbor.
Behold, I am against the prophets who cast out prophecies of the tongue and doze their own dozing.

Behold, I am against the prophets who prophesy false dreams, who told them and led My people astray by their lies and wanderings. I did not send or command them, and they will bring this people no benefit at all.
And if this people, a priest, or a prophet asks you, What is the Lord’s burden? say to them, You are the burden, and I will dash you down, says the Lord.
but, As the Lord lives, who gathered all Israel’s offspring from the northern land and all the countries where He drove them out, and restored them to their land.
Among the prophets my heart was shattered; within me all my bones were shaken. I became like a shattered man, like a person gripped by wine, before the Lord and the splendor of His glory.
Has abandoning Me not brought these things upon you? says the Lord your God.
Now what do you have to do with Egypt’s road, to drink Gihon’s water? And what do you have to do with the Assyrians’ road, to drink river waters?
Your apostasy will discipline you, and your evil will rebuke you. Know and see that abandoning Me is bitter for you, says the Lord your God; and I took no pleasure in you, says the Lord your God.

not according to the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took their hand to bring them out of Egypt’s land, because they did not remain in My covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.

Because this is the covenant I will make with Israel’s house after those days, says the Lord: I will surely put My laws into their understanding and write them upon their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be My people.

And they will certainly not teach each his fellow citizen or his brother, saying, Know the Lord, because they will all know Me, from their least to their greatest. I will be merciful toward their injustices and certainly remember their sins no more.
If the heaven is raised to the height, says the Lord, and the earth’s ground lowered beneath, even then I do not reject Israel’s family, says the Lord, for all they did.

If a man sends his wife away, and she leaves him and becomes another man’s, surely she will not return to him again? Would not that woman be utterly polluted? And you prostituted yourself with many shepherds—and were you returning to Me? says the Lord.
In all these things faithless Judah did not return to Me with her whole heart, but in falsehood.
The Lord said to me, Israel has justified himself in comparison with faithless Judah.

Go and read these words toward the north: Return to Me, dwelling of Israel, says the Lord. I will not set My face firmly against you, because I am merciful, says the Lord, and I will not be angry with you for ever.
Lift your eyes straight ahead and see: where have you not been defiled? You sat for them on the roads like a solitary crow, and polluted the land with your prostitution and your evils.
You had many shepherds as a stumbling block for yourself. You had a prostitute’s appearance; you were shameless toward everyone.
therefore hear the Lord’s word. Thus said the Lord: If you set your faces toward Egypt and go in to live there,
the sword you fear will find you in Egypt’s land, and the famine you are concerned about will catch up with you from behind in Egypt, and there you will die.
All the people and all the foreigners who set their faces toward Egypt’s land to live there will perish by sword and famine. None of them will be saved from the calamities I am bringing upon them.
The king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, and he slaughtered all Judah’s rulers at Deblatha.
He blinded Zedekiah’s eyes and bound him in fetters. The king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in a mill house until the day he died.
In the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuzaradan, the chief guard who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
He burned the Lord’s house, the king’s house, and all the city’s houses; every great house he burned with fire.
The Chaldean force with the chief guard pulled down the whole wall of Jerusalem all around.
There were ninety-six pomegranates on one side; all the pomegranates around the net numbered one hundred.
The chief guard took the first priest, the second priest, and the three men guarding the road,

and one eunuch who supervised the warriors, seven prominent men in the king’s presence who were found in the city, the scribe of the forces who kept records for the people of the land, and sixty people from the people of the land found inside the city.
Nebuzaradan, the chief guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Deblatha,
and the king of Babylon struck them at Deblatha in Aimath’s land.

In the thirty-seventh year after Ioakim king of Judah had been deported, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fourth of the month, Oulaimaradach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, took up the head of Ioakim king of Judah and brought him out of the house where he was guarded.
On the ninth of the month, the famine grew severe in the city, and there were no loaves for the people of the land.

The city was breached, and all the warriors went out at night by the gate between the wall and the outer wall beside the king’s garden, while the Chaldeans surrounded the city. They went by the road to Arabah,
and the Chaldean force pursued the king and overtook him beyond Jericho. All his servants scattered away from him.
They captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Deblatha, and he spoke to him in judgment.

target_units.text: And within it was something like a likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: a human likeness was upon them,
and each had four faces, and each had four wings.

full_triples.rationale: In both visions the wheels accompany the creatures as they move and rise from the earth. The later scene adds that the wheels did not turn when the cherubim raised their wings.
full_triples.source_text: When the cherubim went, the wheels went beside them. When the cherubim raised their wings to rise from the earth, their wheels did not turn.

target_units.text: When the living creatures went, the wheels moved beside them; when the living creatures rose from the earth, the wheels rose.

full_triples.rationale: Both accounts synchronize the standing and rising of creatures and wheels and explain their movement by a spirit of life. The earlier account explicitly locates that spirit in the wheels.
full_triples.source_text: When they stood, these stood; when they rose, these rose with them, because a spirit of life was in them.

target_units.text: Wherever the cloud was, there was the spirit for movement; the living creatures and the wheels went and rose together with them, because a spirit of life was in the wheels.
When they went, these went; when they stood, these stood; when they rose from the earth, these rose together with them, because a spirit of life was in the wheels.

full_triples.rationale: The glory leaves the house and mounts the cherubim here. The following chapter continues its departure from the city to the mountain opposite it, tracing the successive locations of the same glory.
full_triples.source_text: The Lord’s glory went out from the house and mounted upon the cherubim,

target_units.text: The cherubim raised their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was upon them, above them.
The Lord’s glory rose from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain opposite the city.

full_triples.rationale: The cherubim and glory stand at the opposite gate of the Lord's house. The next scene brings Ezekiel to that opposite gate and specifies its eastward orientation.
full_triples.source_text: and the cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the earth before me as they went out, with the wheels beside them. They stood at the entrance of the opposite gate of the Lord’s house, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
