full_triples.rationale: Ezekiel expressly identifies these cherubim with the creature beneath Israel's God at Chebar. The first chapter locates his divine vision by that river and introduces the living creatures within it.
full_triples.source_text: This is the living creature I had seen beneath the God of Israel at the river Chebar, and I knew that it was cherubim.

target_units.text: And it happened in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth of the month, while I was among the captives by the River Chebar: the heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.
On the fifth of the month—this was the fifth year of King Jehoiakim’s captivity—
the Lord’s word came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the River Chebar; and the Lord’s hand came upon me,

and I looked, and behold, a sweeping wind was coming from the north, and a great cloud was within it, with brightness around it and fire flashing like lightning; within it was something like the appearance of electrum, within the fire, and brightness within it.
And within it was something like a likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: a human likeness was upon them,
and each had four faces, and each had four wings.

full_triples.rationale: Both descriptions give the creatures four faces and human hands beneath their wings. The supplied counts differ: this unit says eight wings each, while the earlier unit says four; neither count is harmonized.
full_triples.source_text: Each had four faces, each had eight wings, and the likeness of human hands was beneath their wings.

target_units.text: and each had four faces, and each had four wings.
Their legs were straight, and their feet were winged, with sparks like flashing bronze; and their wings were light.
A human hand was beneath their wings on their four sides; and the faces of all four of them
did not turn as they walked; each went straight ahead.

full_triples.rationale: The later faces are explicitly identified with those seen at Chebar, and the straight-ahead movement recurs. The earlier passage describes the faces and repeats that the creatures do not turn as they go.
full_triples.source_text: As for the likeness of their faces, these are the faces I had seen beneath the glory of the God of Israel at the river Chebar; each of them went straight ahead.

target_units.text: A human hand was beneath their wings on their four sides; and the faces of all four of them
did not turn as they walked; each went straight ahead.
The likeness of their faces was a human face and a lion’s face on the right for all four, and a calf’s face on the left for all four, and an eagle’s face for all four.
The wings of all four were stretched out above; each had two joined to one another, and two covered the top of their bodies.
Each went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit was going, they went and did not turn.

full_triples.rationale: A spirit lifts Ezekiel and brings him to a temple gate in each scene. The earlier transport reaches the inner gate facing north, while this scene identifies the opposite gate facing east.
full_triples.source_text: A spirit lifted me and brought me to the opposite gate of the Lord’s house, facing east. And behold, at the gate entrance were about twenty-five men. Among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Ezer and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.

target_units.text: He stretched out the likeness of a hand and lifted me by the crown of my head. A spirit lifted me between earth and heaven and brought me to Jerusalem in a vision of God, to the entrance of the inner gate facing north, where the pillar of the one acquiring stood.

full_triples.rationale: The city's leaders are accused of devising vain things and counseling wicked counsel. Micah likewise condemns people who plan evil before carrying it out, naming their coveting of fields and their oppression and plundering of households and inheritance.
full_triples.source_text: The Lord said to me, “Son of man, these are the men who devise vain things and counsel wicked counsel in this city,

target_units.text: They became people planning troubles and working evil on their beds, and at daybreak they carried them out, because they did not raise their hands to God.
They coveted fields and plundered orphans, oppressed houses and plundered a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.

full_triples.rationale: The leaders call the city a cauldron and themselves meat. The later parable uses a cauldron containing cuts of meat against the city of bloodshed, turning the same kind of image into a judgment scene.
full_triples.source_text: who say, ‘Have the houses not been built recently? She is the cauldron, and we are the meat.’

and put the cut pieces into it, every good cut, leg and shoulder stripped from the bones,
from choice animals taken. Burn the bones beneath them. It boiled, it boiled, and her bones have been cooked within her.
Therefore thus says the Lord: O city of bloodshed! A cauldron with rust in it, whose rust has not come out of her! He brought it out limb by limb; no lot fell upon her.

full_triples.rationale: The Lord declares that He understands Israel's inner deliberations. David's charge to Solomon likewise says the Lord examines every heart and knows every thought, grounding both passages in divine knowledge of inward motives.
full_triples.source_text: The Lord’s spirit fell upon me, and He said to me, “Say, ‘Thus says the Lord: You have said this, house of Israel, and I understand the deliberations of your spirit.

target_units.text: And now, Solomon my son, know the God of your fathers, and serve Him with a whole heart and a willing soul; for the Lord examines every heart and knows every thought. If you seek Him, He shall be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you utterly.

full_triples.rationale: The leaders have multiplied the city's dead and filled its roads with wounded people. Chapter 22 similarly indicts the city for shedding blood within itself and becoming guilty through that bloodshed.
full_triples.source_text: You have multiplied your dead in this city and filled her roads with the wounded.

target_units.text: and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: O city shedding blood within her so that her time may come, making reflections against herself to defile herself!

full_triples.source_text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Your dead whom you struck within her are the meat, and she is the cauldron; but I will bring you out of her.

full_triples.rationale: Both oracles say that the very sword feared by the hearers will come upon them. Jeremiah directs the warning to people seeking safety in Egypt; Ezekiel addresses the city's leaders.
full_triples.source_text: You fear the sword, and I will bring a sword upon you, says the Lord.

target_units.text: the sword you fear will find you in Egypt’s land, and the famine you are concerned about will catch up with you from behind in Egypt, and there you will die.

full_triples.rationale: The threatened removal into foreigners' hands for judgment has a narrative counterpart in Jerusalem's priests, officials and people being taken to Babylon's king and struck at Deblatha. The passages describe judgment following removal from the city.
full_triples.source_text: I will bring you out of her midst, hand you into foreigners’ hands, and execute judgments among you.

target_units.text: The chief guard took the first priest, the second priest, and the three men guarding the road,

and one eunuch who supervised the warriors, seven prominent men in the king’s presence who were found in the city, the scribe of the forces who kept records for the people of the land, and sixty people from the people of the land found inside the city.
Nebuzaradan, the chief guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Deblatha,
and the king of Babylon struck them at Deblatha in Aimath’s land.

full_triples.rationale: The city will not be a cauldron with these leaders as its meat. The earlier correction has already assigned that image to their victims and announced that the leaders themselves would be brought out.
full_triples.source_text: She will not be a cauldron for you, and you certainly will not become meat within her. At Israel’s borders I will judge you,

target_units.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Your dead whom you struck within her are the meat, and she is the cauldron; but I will bring you out of her.

full_triples.rationale: Pelatiah's death prompts Ezekiel to fall on his face and cry over the possible end of Israel's survivors. His earlier response to the city's slaughter uses the same posture and concern for the remnant.
full_triples.source_text: As I prophesied, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. I fall upon my face and cried aloud with a loud voice and said, “Alas, alas, Lord! Thou art bringing Israel’s survivors to a complete end!”

target_units.text: As they struck, I fall upon my face and cried aloud and said, “Alas, Lord! Art Thou obliterating the survivors of Israel as Thou pourest out Thy wrath upon Jerusalem?”

full_triples.rationale: Jerusalem's inhabitants claim the land while excluding the captives. The later inhabitants of devastated places likewise claim possession, arguing from Abraham and their greater numbers; both speeches assert entitlement within judgment settings.
full_triples.source_text: “Son of man, your brothers and the men of your captivity and the whole house of Israel have been brought to an end. To them Jerusalem’s inhabitants said, ‘Keep far from the Lord; the land has been given to us as an inheritance.’

target_units.text: “Son of man, those dwelling in the devastated places upon Israel’s land say, ‘Abraham was one, yet he possessed the land. We are more; the land has been given to us as a possession.’

full_triples.rationale: God promises to be a little sanctuary to those scattered abroad. Moses' prayer likewise calls the Lord the people's refuge through every generation, locating shelter in God Himself rather than a particular dwelling place.
full_triples.source_text: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will thrust them away into the nations and scatter them through all the earth, and I will be a little sanctuary for them in the countries where they may enter.’

target_units.text: A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, Thou becamest our refuge through every generation.
Before the mountains came to be and the earth and inhabited world were formed, from age to age Thou art.

full_triples.rationale: Both promises gather the scattered people from the nations and lands and bring them into their own land. The later formulation restates the return promised to the displaced people here.
full_triples.source_text: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will receive them from the nations and gather them from the countries where I scattered them, and I will give them the land of Israel.

target_units.text: I will take you out of the nations, gather you out of all the lands and bring you into your own land.

full_triples.rationale: Removal of the land's abominations accompanies the people's return. The later restoration similarly ends defilement by idols and joins deliverance from lawless deeds with cleansing.
full_triples.source_text: They will enter there and remove all her abominations and all her lawlessness from her.

target_units.text: so that they no longer defile themselves with their idols. I will deliver them from all their lawless deeds in which they sinned and cleanse them. They will be My people, and I, the Lord, will be their God.

full_triples.rationale: Both promises replace the heart of stone with a heart of flesh and give a new spirit. The earlier says another heart, while the later says a new heart, preserving each formulation.
full_triples.source_text: I will give them another heart and put a new spirit within them. I will tear the stone heart from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,

target_units.text: And I will give you a new heart, and I will give a new spirit within you; and I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh, and give you a heart of flesh.

full_triples.rationale: Both passages connect inner renewal with keeping God's ordinances and conclude that the people will be His and He will be their God. The later passage explicitly says His Spirit enables that obedience.
full_triples.source_text: so that they may walk in My commands, keep My ordinances and carry them out. They will be My people, and I will be their God.

target_units.text: I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments and do them.
You will dwell upon the land I gave your fathers. You will be My people, and I will be your God.

full_triples.rationale: God brings the people's ways upon their heads in both judgments. Here the explanation names hearts directed toward abominations and lawlessness; the earlier verdict accompanies the city's execution scene.
full_triples.source_text: As their heart went toward the heart of their abominations and their lawlessness, I have brought their ways upon their heads, says the Lord.’”

target_units.text: My eye will not spare, nor will I have mercy. I have brought their ways upon their heads.”

full_triples.rationale: The cherubim again raise their wings with wheels beside them and the divine glory above them. The preceding scene gives the same arrangement as they rise from the earth toward the gate.
full_triples.source_text: The cherubim raised their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was upon them, above them.

full_triples.rationale: The glory leaves the city and stands on the opposite mountain. In the later vision it comes by the eastern gate and fills the house again, creating a departure-and-return correspondence without naming the earlier mountain.
full_triples.source_text: The Lord’s glory rose from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain opposite the city.

target_units.text: He led me to the gate facing east and brought me out.

Look—the glory of the God of Israel was coming by the way of the gate facing east. The sound of the camp was like the sound of many redoubling their sound, and the earth flashed like radiance from the glory all around.
The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when I was entering to anoint the city; and the vision of the chariot I saw was like the vision I had seen by the River Chobar. I fall on my face.
The glory of the Lord entered the house by the way of the gate facing east.
A spirit lifted me and brought me into the inner court. Look—the house was full of the glory of the Lord.

full_triples.rationale: The Spirit brings Ezekiel back to the captives in Chaldea as the vision ends. The earlier transport had brought him to Jerusalem in a divine vision, supplying the outward movement answered by this return.
full_triples.source_text: A spirit lifted me and brought me into the Chaldeans’ land, to the captives, in a vision by God’s spirit. I rose out of the vision I had seen,

target_units.text: He stretched out the likeness of a hand and lifted me by the crown of my head. A spirit lifted me between earth and heaven and brought me to Jerusalem in a vision of God, to the entrance of the inner gate facing north, where the pillar of the one acquiring stood.

full_triples.rationale: Ezekiel reports to the captives all the Lord's words shown to him. This carries out his commission to speak God's words to the embittering house.
full_triples.source_text: and I spoke to the captives all the Lord’s words that He had shown me.

target_units.text: You will speak My words to them, if indeed they listen or are terrified, for it is an embittering house.

full_triples.rationale: Both indict the people for having eyes without seeing and ears without hearing. Ezekiel associates that refusal with the embittering house, while Jeremiah calls his audience foolish and senseless.
full_triples.source_text: “Son of man, you dwell in the midst of their injustices. They have eyes to see and do not see, and ears to hear and do not hear, because they are an embittering house.

target_units.text: Hear these things now, foolish and senseless people: they have eyes and do not see; they have ears and do not hear.

full_triples.rationale: The commanded preparation of captivity belongings is interpreted later as a portent of the people's deportation. The explanation directly connects Ezekiel's enacted departure with what will happen to them.
full_triples.source_text: And you, son of man, get your belongings ready for captivity by day before them. You will be taken captive from your place to another place before them, so that they may see, because they are an embittering house.

target_units.text: Say, ‘I perform portents in her midst. As I have done, so it will be for them; in deportation and captivity they will go.’

full_triples.rationale: The command distinguishes bringing belongings out by day and departing in the evening. Ezekiel's report reproduces that sequence as he performs the sign before the people.
full_triples.source_text: You will bring your belongings out like belongings for captivity by day before their eyes, and you yourself will go out in the evening as a captive goes out.

target_units.text: I did so according to all that He commanded me. I brought belongings out like belongings for captivity by day; in the evening I dug through the wall for myself and went out concealed. I was lifted upon shoulders before them.

full_triples.rationale: Digging through the wall in the enacted sign corresponds to the ruler's predicted concealed departure through the wall. The later unit explains the public action in terms of the ruler's fate.
full_triples.source_text: Before them, dig for yourself through the wall, and you will pass out through it.

target_units.text: The ruler among them will be lifted upon shoulders and go out concealed through the wall. He will dig through it to go out through it. He will cover his face so that he may not be seen by an eye, and he himself will not see the land.

full_triples.rationale: Being lifted upon shoulders, departing concealed and covering the face recur in the prediction concerning the ruler. Both units also state that the covered person will not see the land.
full_triples.source_text: Before them you will be lifted upon shoulders and go out concealed. Cover your face, and you certainly will not see the land, for I have made you a portent to the house of Israel.”

full_triples.rationale: Ezekiel performs the commanded deportation sign before the people. A later symbolic action is likewise explained by saying Ezekiel is their portent and that what he has done will happen to them, though the enacted actions differ.
full_triples.source_text: I did so according to all that He commanded me. I brought belongings out like belongings for captivity by day; in the evening I dug through the wall for myself and went out concealed. I was lifted upon shoulders before them.

full_triples.source_text: “Son of man, has not the house of Israel, the embittering house, said to you, ‘What are you doing?’

full_triples.rationale: The sign announces that the people will go into deportation and captivity. Kings recounts the removal of the remaining city population and those who had gone over to Babylon's king.
full_triples.source_text: Say, ‘I perform portents in her midst. As I have done, so it will be for them; in deportation and captivity they will go.’

full_triples.source_text: The ruler among them will be lifted upon shoulders and go out concealed through the wall. He will dig through it to go out through it. He will cover his face so that he may not be seen by an eye, and he himself will not see the land.

and the Chaldean force pursued the king and overtook him beyond Jericho. All his servants scattered away from him.
They captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Deblatha, and he spoke to him in judgment.

full_triples.rationale: The ruler is to be caught, brought to Babylon, unable to see it, and die there. Jeremiah narrates Zedekiah's capture, blinding and removal to Babylon, where he remained in a mill house until his death.
full_triples.source_text: I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My enclosure. I will bring him to Babylon, to the Chaldeans’ land, and he will not see it, and there he will die.

full_triples.rationale: The threat scatters the ruler's helpers and supporters. Jeremiah's account of the king's capture explicitly says all his servants scattered away from him.
full_triples.source_text: All those around him, his helpers and all who support him, I will scatter to every wind; I will draw a sword after them.

full_triples.rationale: Both passages announce scattering among the nations and lands as divine judgment. Leviticus places that dispersal among the covenant penalties, alongside sword and desolation.
full_triples.source_text: They will know that I am the Lord when I scatter them among the nations, and I will disperse them among the countries.

target_units.text: And I will scatter you among the nations, and the advancing sword shall consume you. Your land shall become desolate, and your cities shall be desolate.

full_triples.rationale: Both passages preserve survivors of judgment among the nations and connect their survival with acknowledgment of the Lord and their abominations. Here they recount their lawlessness; the earlier passage emphasizes remembrance and grief.
full_triples.source_text: I will spare a few men among them from sword, famine and death, so that they may recount all their lawlessness among the nations where they entered, and they will know that I am the Lord.”

target_units.text: When there are among you survivors of the sword among the nations, and in your scattering in the lands,

the survivors from among you will remember Me among the nations where they were taken captive. I have sworn against their heart that whores away from Me and their eyes that whore after their pursuits; they will beat their faces over all their abominations.
They will recognize that I, the Lord, have spoken.

full_triples.rationale: The enacted eating and drinking in pain and distress corresponds to the earlier announcement of Jerusalem's measured bread and water in need and devastation. Both make bodily deprivation part of the siege warning.
full_triples.source_text: “Son of man, eat your bread with pain, and drink your water with torment and distress,

target_units.text: He said to me, “Son of man, behold, I am breaking the support of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight and in need, and drink water by measure and in devastation,
so that they become needy for bread and water. A man and his brother will disappear, and they will waste away in their injustices.

full_triples.rationale: Jerusalem's inhabitants will eat bread in want. The covenant warning similarly describes scarce bread distributed by weight and eaten without satisfaction; Ezekiel also includes distressed water and the land's devastation.
full_triples.source_text: and say to the people of the land, ‘Thus says the Lord to Jerusalem’s inhabitants upon Israel’s land: They will eat their bread with want and drink their water with devastation, so that the land may be destroyed with its fullness, for all who dwell in it are in impiety.

target_units.text: When I afflict you with a scarcity of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven and give back your bread by weight. You shall eat and in no wise be filled.

full_triples.rationale: Both announcements join desolate cities with a wasted land. Leviticus supplies the covenant-warning setting, while Ezekiel declares the coming condition of the inhabited cities.
full_triples.source_text: Their inhabited cities will be made desolate, and the land will be laid waste. You will recognize that I am the Lord.’”

target_units.text: and I will make your cities desolate, and lay waste your holy places; and I will in no wise smell the savour of your sacrifices;
and I Myself will desolate your land, and your enemies who dwell in it shall marvel at it.
And I will scatter you among the nations, and the advancing sword shall consume you. Your land shall become desolate, and your cities shall be desolate.

full_triples.rationale: The proverb about distant days and a perished vision is restated as the claim that Ezekiel speaks of far-off times. The two formulations expose the audience's dismissal of the warning's immediacy.
full_triples.source_text: “Son of man, what is this proverb you have concerning Israel’s land, saying, ‘The days are far off; vision has perished’?

target_units.text: “Son of man, behold, the embittering house of Israel keeps saying, ‘The vision this man sees is for many days ahead; this man prophesies of times far ahead.’

full_triples.source_text: Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will turn back this proverb, and the house of Israel certainly will no longer say this proverb.’ For you will speak to them: ‘The days have drawn near, and the word of every vision,

full_triples.rationale: The end of false visions and pleasing divination corresponds to Zechariah's promise to remove false prophets and the unclean spirit from the land. Both anticipate the removal of deceptive religious speech.
full_triples.source_text: because there will no longer be any false vision or anyone divining pleasing things among the sons of Israel,

target_units.text: On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the idols’ names from the land, and there will no longer be remembrance of them. I will remove the false prophets and the unclean spirit from the land.

full_triples.rationale: The Lord promises to speak and act without further delay. Balaam's declaration similarly asks whether God could speak and fail to act or abide by His word; it supports the certainty of action without supplying Ezekiel's timetable.
full_triples.source_text: because I, the Lord, will speak My words; I will speak and act, and I certainly will delay no longer. For in your days, embittering house, I will speak a word and act, says the Lord.’”

target_units.text: God is not as a man, to be led astray, nor as a son of man, to be threatened; having spoken, shall He not act? Shall He speak, and not abide by it?
